It is done. The altars scream with what you’ve torn from them—fragments of truth, drenched in blood. I see it clearly now: the curse’s origins lie not in flesh or stone, but in forces that reach beyond our understanding. The answers we’ve uncovered are but whispers of what’s to come. You’ve walked a path few dare tread, but the journey is not over. You must decide if you’ll face what lies ahead. The weight of this choice will be yours alone to bear.

Hm. A disturbing sight reveals itself. A guardian bound by magical chains... the one within the frost. It seems to be watching over the vessel that sustains the curse. Adventurer, seek out that creature and uncover the truth it hides. But be wary. This cold conceals far more than you realize.
You truly made the shadows come alive in there... and I bet those following you couldn’t even see what was coming for them!
That will show them! I don’t expect to hear any more stories about spiders haunting the halls of that cursed castle... Thanks again for all your efforts.
Finally! It took you long enough! I hope you kept the wings in one piece. Either way, these should do the trick.
These will do just the trick! Capturing these dreams is sure to unlock their secrets—and perhaps, bring you great fortune as well.
Yes! This is just what I needed to glimpse the other side... Oh, and here! Take this.
The treasure was yours from the start, aren’t you glad you trusted me! You’re special, and I surely wouldn’t guide anyone else.
I told you, a little luck can make anything easier! The path may seem clear now, but I can’t shake an uneasy feeling about what lies ahead...

Mmm... a powerful presence lingers here. The sound of waves, and faint whispers left behind... If your inner eye were open, you too might hear them one day. And now, I must do what I can with this. Seek the paths that have yet to be revealed...

Hmm... this is a very old kind of magic. Both the necklace and the fragment carry similar traces. This enchantment protects its bearer and strengthens the bond of trust between them. It seems well-suited to bind a tribe together as one. But I will need to study it further before I can say more.
Well done, adventurer. The warden sleeps, and you have endured the trial of the tides. Now the sea shall remember your name...
This aura of the demon... For an ordinary soul, merely being near it would bring peril... First, we must cleanse the ominous fluids that shroud it. You have done well.
The aura that emanates from here... it feels like evil itself. I have never encountered anything quite like it before. Yet it may be the only thread by which hope can be reclaimed.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_FortuneTeller_Gree: The whispers are growing louder, their cadence sharp and desperate, yet they remain beyond our grasp. The dead do not merely wish to be heard—they crave a voice to speak through. To bridge the chasm between our realm and theirs, we must bind the tangible to the ethereal. The tongue of a mimic, that vile creature born of deception, holds the power to weave words across worlds. Seek out one of these lurking horrors, wrest its tongue from its snapping maw, and bring it to me. Only then can we compel the dead to answer.

The threads of fate twist and knot, veiling truths beyond our mortal sight. I have glimpsed a shadow, vast and formless, threatening to engulf the fragile balance of our world. Yet, my visions falter, shrouded in mist. We need a catalyst—something to pierce the veil. Deep within the cursed woods, the dire wolves prowl, their eyes glinting with unnatural light. One of their eyes must be extracted while the warmth of life still lingers—a gruesome act, but necessary. Bring me this eyeball, stained by blood, and together we shall unravel the first strand of this enigma.

The eye failed us; its vision clouded... Sight has betrayed me, adventurer, but perhaps sound will not. The voices of the dead echo faintly, yearning to be heard. Deep within the caverns, the giant bats dwell, their ears attuned to the faintest of vibrations, even those that ripple from the beyond. Sever one ear from these shadowed predators—bloodied and raw—and bring it to me. Only then may we align with the spectral murmurs that seek to guide us.

Deep in the Icicle Cave lies a creature—not just a beast, but a sentinel tied to the curse’s very essence. Those who sent you here—my peers—they suspect its existence, and they are not wrong. But this guardian won’t reveal itself easily. Its servants, kobolds twisted by frost magic, will try to stop you. Bring me proof of their presence—primitive bracelets—and uncover what it is that this guardian protects. The truth is within reach, but beware: even knowledge can cut deeper than a blade.

You’ve uncovered the cursed, their guardians, and their chains. Now you must take the final step—one that will demand more from you than any blade or spell. The Altar of Sacrifice, steeped in dark rituals, are tied to the curse’s power. They must be used—three times—to unravel the threads that bind this blight to our world. Know this: each use of the altar comes at a cost, and its echoes will follow you. But this is the only way to uncover the heart of the curse. Will you accept this burden, adventurer?

Those who foresaw an ill-fated future, peers of mine in their own ways, have sent you to me. They understand that this curse is no simple illness. To break it, one must look beyond the limits of human sight. Bring me the items that allow a glimpse of the truth hidden in the dark. But be warned. Do not look into them too deeply.

The Forgotten Castle appears to be well lit... well, let's change that. I need you to darken the place, and then once it is done you can use the shadows to aid you in taking care of anyone that intends to do you harm.

When you visited the castle... Did you see them? Spiders are everywhere. I heard some rooms are so bad, you can’t walk without them biting at your ankles. They crawl out from those wretched pots that have been sitting in the castle untouched for years! If you destroy enough of those pots, it might send those spiders back into hiding for good.

The bats in this area are unlike any other... if you bring me two of their wings I’ll prove it to you! Just be careful, you aren’t the only adventurer on this journey... but you must be the first to complete it.

Lately I have had dreams that send chills down my spine... If only I could catch them, I might uncover their true meaning. Maybe you could help me do just that... but I will need some materials that only an adventurer like you can obtain.
I need one more thing... and I know it won’t be easy to obtain, but with a few Luck Potions, however, you might manage it. Bring me a Wendigo Hoof, I will make it worth your time!

The Frost Mountain is known to have piles of treasure, but only the most daring adventurers have ever set their sights on them. That will be no problem for you though! Trust me, I have already seen your success.

The late king installed Wall Spikes throughout The Forgotten Castle to keep wanderers away. With a little luck, I believe you could disarm them for safe passage. Just remember, sometimes, you have to create your own luck.

There are things that grow only in the harsh reaches of the Blue Maelstrom. Among them, the Saltvine... is not consumed by the mouth, but by the mind. The Tidewalkers have known this truth since ancient days. When they perform their rites, they burn the vine and breathe its smoke. Adventurer, bring me a few strands of it as well. The time has come to kindle a new smoke.

Surviving the tempestuous sea is no small matter, even for monsters. It is said the Tidewalkers place enchanted necklaces upon the warriors who return from the maelstrom, gifts woven with a shaman's blessing. The warrior protects the shaman, and the shaman shields the tribe. I wonder what truths lie hidden within such a blessing. I will need a few items, worn and weathered by their hands.

The great white shark is both warden and judge of the sea. If you intend to keep venturing out upon the waters, you must beware of them. These beasts show no mercy to those who trespass into their domain. Strike them down before they sink their teeth into you. I know you can do it. The stars shine upon your path. Now go, adventurer... and bring me the spoils of your victory.

Demons with wicked souls and their hounds guard every corner of the Inferno... Because of them, we have yet to truly gaze into its depths... To draw even a little closer to the secrets of that dreadful place, I require an item bound to it. Could you bring me something tied to those fiends?

The item you brought last time proved most helpful. Yet to examine the depths of the Inferno more closely, I require more wicked relics bound to that place. If you aid me, we shall draw one step closer to uncovering the source of this evil. Clear away all that stands in your path.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_GoblinMerchant_Com: Huzzah! Well done, me fleshy friend. Those green skins didn’t know what hit ‘em! Ahh, there’s trouble brewin’. You see, me kin be stirred up now, all riled and angry. They’ll retaliate, mark me words... But with you, my fleshy friend, we boom boom bop 'em and they learns not to mess with Gobbo again!

No, no, no, no... This isn’t right. My... my precious fleshy, the one who always protected me, they’re gone. Torn apart like they were nothing! Grrr... My kin will pay for this—every last one of them! Their ears will be my trophies! You hear me, fleshy? This gobbo’s gonna make them regret ever laying a hand on mine! Kurikuri goblins... Remember my words!

Good, good! I like this! You... you might just become gobbo’s new precious fleshy... Hehe. Look at that—eight shiny goblin ears, stacked up nice and pretty. Hehehe, those filthy green-skins don’t even know what hit ‘em! Right now, their pride? It’s mine. Well done, squishy friend. But this isn’t the end. Oh no, my kin still have lessons to learn... and it’s gonna be real rough for them.

Aha! That’s the one! You did it, fleshy friend! That’s the shell I needed for my glorious goblin stew. It’s feast time! And as promised, here’s a little secret—about the missing girl... She’s not what she seems, friend. It’s not just that she disappeared—there’s something more. But that’s all I can say for now. If you want the truth, you’ll have to dig deeper yourself. For now, let’s eat, and just remember—this gobbo always keeps his promises! Hehehe!

Ha! That’s more like it! The mage won’t be talkin’ down on my Famous Grubs stew ever again, no sir! And with the centipedes and spiders you bopped, me next batch’s gonna be fit for a gob king! Me kin will eat those words, heh-heh, next time, they’ll beg for more! You did good, fleshy—me’ll make sure your shiny reward just as special as me stew. Hee-hee!

Yahoo! You found the cursed escape route! We’re one step closer now, fleshy friend. Look, Gobbo’s been preparing something bigger than they could ever imagine. My kin will pay for every single thing they did to me. Trust Gobbo, fleshy—the time is coming soon... Gobbo’s big plan is gonna be way bigger than they expect—whoosh-BOOM! Hehehe!

Oh, now that’s tough. And a lot... bigger than I expected? Hrm, alright, it looks tasty. I like it, I really do! Might be better for something other than stew though... hmm, I’ll have to think on it. Meat lump, once it's done, I’ll let you know. I might even give you a bite, since it’s you.
So? Find anything good in there? Gonna give some to me? Nah, keep it all. There’s something else I want anyway. Come back when you’ve got time! I’ll tell you what I’m really looking for!

Yes! This is it! I knew you’d bring the right thing, fleshy! Gobbo’s eyes never lie! Haha! To think I get to eat this again. Gotta let it cool first. Gobbo’s luck never runs out. Huh? You asking if I’m eating it? Of course! Want a bite?
Bash! Bash! Bash! Musta been fun! Wish I coulda join in wid ya.
Oho, still nice and warm! But these one’s are all black like that. Didn’t it burn completely? Even better! I’ll slip it right into their stew. Hehe. Eat this, you fools!
Dem gobbo heads smashed betta than those crates! Dat’ll show em whos da real bossman!
Huzzah! How ya open them big metal boxes. Me thought all dem shinies safe in dere.
Yum! Centipede legs are crunchy delight. Here sum junk to make it a gud trade.
Wowza! You a gobbo hero. Dun get comfy cuz dere be more dangers in da caves!
Huzzah! With dis lucky feather, me fortunes sure ta change!
Ooh! Lots of shinies! Hopefully no ghoulies followed you back.

Alright, friend. You’re finally looking a bit better. While you were getting rid of the bad stuff, I managed to score a little something myself. Actually, you ended up tossing out my bad luck too. Heh. So, I suppose I owe you something shiny. Not bad, right?

Well done! I have no idea why they treasured that junk, but now that both are gone, they’ll be searching for quite some time. Just thinking about it is amusing! Now, those fools will take out their frustration on those infuriating green-skins for me!
That’s right, fleshling! I knew I could count on you! You know what the most obvious truth in the world is? You are useful to this goblin—they are not!
What? They had a lot of weapons? How many—piled up like a stockpile? Hmm, that is strange. What are they planning...? Thanks, fleshling! I’ll take it from here and dig deeper!
Good good, you did real good! Perfect! Shame me not see their stupid faces all squished on floor, hah! But anyway, from today, you my most precious fleshthing! Hehehe!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_GoblinMerchant_Gre: Ah, my brilliant fleshy! The one who’ll take care of my wretched kin! Ha! Me? I was cast out of the caves, abandoned by my own kind! Those brainless green-skins—bah! My tribe thinks I wasted my time making fleshy friends and collecting shinies. They’re too stupid to see what truly matters. But me? I’m smart. Hehe. Let’s see how they fare without this gobbo! Now, get in that cave and give those traitors a proper beating! Don’t worry, fleshy friend—I’ll make sure your effort is worth it. Hehehe!

No! Something is terribly wrong! After we took down the green-skins, my kin went into a frenzy, and now they’ve set their sights on your kind! When I was cast out of the caves, my precious fleshies took me in, fed me, and treated me as more than just a greedy goblin—they treated me as a friend. But now... if they’re no longer here... No! Get inside that wretched prison and find out what’s become of them! Hurry, before it’s too late!

My kin will regret ever laying a hand on my precious fleshy friend. Now, it’s time for gobbo’s revenge! Boom, boom! Look, ears are a goblin’s pride, like a badge of honor. So if we take down those stinking green-skins, we’ll crush their pride! Bring me eight of their ears, and let’s stomp their dignity into the dirt! Hehe! I promise, fleshy—you’ll get a real special reward for your effort! And those goblins? They’ll learn never to mess with this gobbo!

Ahh, fleshy! This time, it’s a different kind of job. Look, all that ruckus I caused? Well, now my gambling buddies are all riled up. They think ol’ gobbo forgot his roots, trying to fit in with fleshy customs. So, I’m gonna show them! I’ll make a special stew—so good, so distracting, they won’t care who I gamble with anymore! But to do that, I need the shell of a certain bug—shiny, tough! You bring me that shell, and maybe... just maybe... I’ll spill a little something about that woman you’re looking for. Something I heard. Hehehe.

Oh! My fleshy friend, listen up! I made a stew with my kin— ‘Gobbos Famous Grubs’! But those stinking green-skins turned their noses up at it, calling it ‘disgusting’! Ha! Fine, now they’re gonna taste gobbo’s fury at full strength! The worst of ‘em was a goblin mage—he mocked me the most. Find him and teach him a lesson! Oh, and while you’re at it, bring me some centipedes and spiders. Then I’ll show you how to make a legendary Famous Grubs that no one will ever forget!

Ughhh! My stew! I can still hear their laughter ringing in my head! I won’t let this go, never! Listen, back when I was exiled, I used a secret path to escape. But that was a long time ago, and I don’t know if it’s still there. I need you to head into the caves and find that escape route for me. I’ve got plans, you see? Plans bigger than they can imagine... bigger than my stew... and when it’s all over, they’ll all say they regret ever crossing Gobbo!

Hey! You heard about it? That new kind of buzzing bug in the caves! Go squash a few of them for me, will ya? I wanna see if they’ll make good stew meat for this gobbo’s next recipe! Heh heh... Flying skulls are no good for nothin’, but these bugs? Now those are juicy little bundles of nutrition!

So the cave went rumble and CRASH, huh?! Hahaha! All the fools who mocked me got what they deserved! I knew it! Down there it’s blazing hot, bright red water flowing everywhere. Don’t touch it, fleshy. Soft meat like yours would burn right up. Those idiots are probably ash by now... so dig through what’s left. Might be something useful, hehehe.

Before I was exiled, I saw it once while wandering the caves. A lizard completely on fire. Just once. It vanished so fast I thought my eyes fooled me, but they didn’t. It left a burning tail behind! Haha! It saw Gobbo and ran off scared. I searched everywhere after that, never saw it again. But I know it’s still out there, in the burning lands.
Me bruddas, always tryna hide me stuff from me. But I know where ta find em. Bash those boxes fer me and I reward ya real nice.

Fleshy, bring me a few mushrooms from the burning lands. Those shrooms grow by drinking that bright red water, so they’re hot. Take one bite and your belly goes up in flames. You’ll be groaning for a week. Gobbo’s kind hates hot stuff, see. That’s why I’m gonna let them have a little taste... secretly!
Oh noes, they ain too happy I busted up their stuff. Me folk tink they smart but we show em. Send em a message that they be messin with the wrong bossman up here.
Shinies? Me think I left too many of me shinies deep in da caves. Get em out for me and I give ya sumthin.
Us green skins face a lotta dangers down in da caves. You wanna get a taste of da goblin life? Tryna dance with some of pets?
That stinky giant is trouble for all gobbo folk. Take em out and make it better for me and me friends!
Me be havin no luck lately. Fetch me a lucky feather from dem nasty birdies to change me luck.
Had some bad luck gamba. Need to replenish my stock. Graves really good for finding good items.

Fleshling! Wait, don’t come any closer. Over there—take a step back! You know it too, right? My luck has been terrible lately. I asked the Fortune teller, and she said I’ve been cursed by bad energy from someone nearby! And you know what? I only have one friend—you. That means you’re the problem. That woman said it—you have to go back to the Ruins. If you want to shake off the misfortune clinging to your back, you have no choice. Again, again, again!

Those wretched green-skins stole my shinies! So, they finally understand their value, huh? But laying their filthy hands on mine—that was a very stupid mistake. Hmph, fools should be left to deal with other fools. Fleshling, go steal some junk from the giants in the cave. And leave this behind. What is it? A stinking rag from those foolish green-skins.

Alright. Last time, the plan was too clever. Looks like the giants just found themselves some new worthless junk to cherish. I completely forgot that those idiots don’t actually think. So this time, we’re going in loud and brutal. Teach those green-skins a lesson for ignoring me. There are plenty of goblin tribes out there—no one’s going to miss a few if they disappear.

Even after the lesson you taught them last time, those wretches are still after my treasure! The same fools who once ignored me over a few shinies! Hey, are you sure you didn’t mess something up when dealing with the green-skins? Why are they acting like this? Ugh, I can’t stand not knowing! Fleshling! Ransack the entire cave! Turn it upside down and leave nothing untouched!

Me look around, me see it real weird. Real real weird! Bad smell, bad plan! Some goblins, real nasty ones, me old tribe. They say "kick him out!" They say "he not goblin enough!" Pah! Now they bossin’ others like they king or something. Why need so many weapons, huh? What for? Big fight? Big boom? Maybe war? Crazy! Crazy like cave bat with fire on tail! Fleshthing, you do it. You smash bad goblins. Break traps too, all of them. Wreck the whole nasty hole!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Goldsmith_Complete: These aren’t bad. Barely good enough for gear of similar quality, perhaps, but they’ll do for practice. Thanks. I’ll be asking you again from time to time.
Very good. This is quite impressive. If you bring your requests to me from now on, I can offer you work of an even higher standard. Well done.
As expected, I knew you wouldn’t disappoint me. I can’t deny that you’ve had a significant impact on improving my craft lately. I look forward to working with you again.
Hm, this is delicious. Where did you get it? ...Somewhere I wouldn’t recognize, you say? Well, as long as it tasted good, that’s enough for me. I’ll be counting on you again next time.
Thank you. This should be more than enough for my research. There’s still plenty I’ll need help with, so please stop by again when you have the time.
Well done. Thanks to you, my storeroom is much better stocked now. I won’t have to worry for a while. Thank you.
By the stars, look at the light passing through this gem. Truly magnificent. My fingers are itching to start working on it right away. I’m glad I asked you, Adventurer.
Truly impressive. With someone like you, Adventurer, I can’t help but believe you’ll one day bring back even legendary gems. Well done.

You’ve brought everything I asked for, just as promised. With such a range of conditions, there’s a great deal to examine. If it weren’t for you, Adventurer, I wouldn’t have even considered trying so many different approaches. You have my sincere thanks.
Such a radiant crimson glow. It truly is different. I know well that chances to work with gemstones like this do not come easily. This is all thanks to you, Adventurer.
You have done well. Every sapphire you brought is in excellent condition. Their balance is already well set, so now it comes down to how carefully I handle them. I will proceed with great care.
I was right to ask you, Adventurer. The materials you brought are in excellent condition. This should be enough to restore my working rhythm.
If crafted properly, there are few gemstones as beautiful as diamonds. They are so hard that there is little need to worry about flaws. Now then, shall we move on to another gemstone?

Thank you very much. If it were not for you, I would never have had the chance to work with such a wide range of gemstones of this quality. If you ever have work you wish to entrust to me, please let me know. I will always give it my highest priority.
Perfect. Opportunities to work with a combination like this are rare. Thanks to you, I can finally attempt a project I had only imagined before. Thank you very much for your help.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Goldsmith_Greeting: Well met! If you’re looking to enhance your gear with gemstones, you’ve come to the right place. There aren’t many gemcutters who can handle both cutting and socketing like I can. Keeping my skills sharp takes constant practice. If you don’t mind, bring me a few gems. A few flaws won’t be a problem.

The quality of a gem has to match the quality of the gear it’s set into. Only then can socketing truly bring out its full power. It’s a demanding craft, so I’m always working to refine my skills. Bring me some gems today. Just make sure they’re of better quality than last time.

Gem socketing is an extremely delicate craft. Lose focus for even a moment, and the whole piece is ruined. Opportunities to work with high-grade gems are rare, which only makes me more particular. That said, do you think you could bring me a few rare gemstones, if possible?

Lately, I’ve been researching whether there might be ways to work with a wider variety of minerals. I knew it wouldn’t be difficult, but it’s proving to be no easy task. That said, after concentrating all day, I’m quite hungry. Sorry to ask, but could you bring me something to eat?

Lately, the demand for silver has been rising. It’s sought after not only by the upper class, but by adventurers as well. I’d like to stock up a bit before it’s too late. My tools are also due for replacement, so if possible, could you bring me some silver along with them? I’d appreciate it.

Gemcrafting requires more tools than you might expect. The ones I use most wear out quickly. I usually keep spares on hand, but it seems I’ve run through a few without noticing. I’ll let you know what I need, so if possible, please bring several of each. Oh, and don’t forget the Rubysilver ingots as well.

I’m confident in my skills, which is why I never want to ruin a job. When I work with rare, high-grade gems, my nerves get so tight it almost makes my stomach ache. I suppose it’s because I’m not used to it yet. There’s no choice but to practice more. For now, please bring me high-quality rubies and diamonds.

Did you know? Every gemstone differs subtly in hardness. Being able to read those differences precisely is one of a gemcutter’s key skills. Now that we’ve worked with rubies and diamonds, it’s time to turn our attention to other gems. Sapphires and emeralds would be ideal. I’ll leave it to you.

Adventurer, I’ve been waiting for you. This time as well, I’d like you to gather some gemstones and minerals for my work. If you happen to come across anything that might be useful for reference in gemcrafting, I’d appreciate it if you could bring that along too. Slightly damaged items are fine, so could you bring several if possible?

I feel that I am ready now. Ready to work with legendary gemstones. It will not be an easy task, of course. Still, the experience I have built up should allow me to focus properly on the work. If you are willing to help me, I could not ask for more. Shall we begin with rubies?

Now that I have warmed up with rubies, sapphires would be a good next step. Sapphires are gemstones where subtle balance matters greatly. A single poor judgment can dull their brilliance. That is why they are well suited for this stage. Please bring me sapphires. The more you can provide, the better.

When you work with similar materials for too long, there comes a moment when the hand grows dull. Like now. At times like this, it helps to handle materials of a different nature for a while. Gold and pearls should be suitable. Please bring ones of decent quality.

Now that my sense of touch has fully returned, I am ready to resume working with legendary gemstones. This time, I would like you to bring me diamonds. Diamonds demand precise angles and restrained polishing. They will help me refine my skills further.

Emeralds are gemstones with an unusually delicate nature among minerals. They may appear hard at first glance, but even a small lapse can leave a mark. That is why delicacy matters more than force when working with them. Could you bring me emeralds this time?

I heard that obsidian can be obtained. That is truly surprising. Obsidian is so rare that it is difficult even to see it in person. If possible, could you bring me some obsidian? The more, the better. I will also need a few materials that suit it. I will write down what is required. I ask this of you.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Huntress_Daily_Com: Not a bad display of skill. You might be ready for something a bit more challenging. I’ll be expecting your next visit.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Huntress_Daily_Gre: I have a strong preference for the capable. Only those kinds of people survive in a place like this. If you're looking for work, I’ve got plenty. But you'd better deliver results.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Huntress_Seasonal_: Not a bad display of skill. You might be ready for something a bit more challenging. I’ll be expecting your next visit.
I have a strong preference for the capable. Only those kinds of people survive in a place like this. If you're looking for work, I’ve got plenty. But you'd better deliver results.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Huntress_Weekly_Co: Not a bad display of skill. You might be ready for something a bit more challenging. I’ll be expecting your next visit.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Huntress_Weekly_Gr: I have a strong preference for the capable. Only those kinds of people survive in a place like this. If you're looking for work, I’ve got plenty. But you'd better deliver results.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_JackOLantern_Compl: Yes, that’s it! At last, these adorable treats will regain their original sweetness. Ah, this scent... I can finally feel my appetite coming back. Thank you so much!

Hmm, since I can’t taste it myself, I can’t quite understand what you mean. Things that aren’t sweet just don’t make sense to me. Speaking of which, would you like some candy? I found it in a dungeon, and it’s absolutely delicious. No? Really? How sad... not to know the joy of such a delightful flavor!
So many candies! All right, now I understand. This is that thrilling taste you were talking about. At last, I understand you. Now it’s my turn to make you happy!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_JackOLantern_Greet: These lovely tricolored candies are a special treat found only this season. But there’s a problem. The old corpses in the dungeons have made the candies taste strange. There’s not a trace of sweetness left! Please, adventurer, get rid of those awful things spoiling the world’s sweetness.

Did you know there’s a kind of taste you don’t feel on your tongue but at your fingertips? They say adventurers like you enjoy that thrill. Some even get addicted, going back to the dungeons again and again. I’m curious, what does it taste like? Will you go and tell me when you return?

Nothing makes the world happier than sweetness. Thanks to you, the cause of that strange taste is gone, so now it’s time to enjoy the real thing. Bring me plenty of delicious candies, and I’ll trade you whatever you want from my collection. They’re of no use to me anyway.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Krampus_Daily_Comp: Good. No more, no less, exactly ten. I’ll take them. I’m looking forward to the next time. You didn’t think this was the end, did you?
Alright, well done. They’ve been wandering around long enough. It’s time for them to rest now. For a very long time.
You made it back. The places you passed through have gotten pretty noisy. I like that. Don’t stop now.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Krampus_Daily_Gree: A festival wouldn’t be complete without a treasure hunt. I’ve hidden my small, adorable treasures all over the place. They make a very clear sound, so they won’t be too hard to find. Just bring me ten. Easy enough, right?
I’m fair to everyone. But festivals are for the living. The dead still shambling around don’t suit this happy season. Would you take care of them for me?
I like those who take action, no matter what. A life spent standing still is boring. So this time, why don’t you do what you enjoy? Wreck every dungeon you can, and make it back alive.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Krampus_Seasonal_C: Here you go. A small, charming reward, fitting for a single Golden Bell. If you want something better, try throwing yourself into the festival a little more.
Not bad. Here’s a reward fitting for five Golden Bells. If you want something more special, you’d better stir up the festival a bit more.
Excellent. You’ve had a truly remarkable winter. I can vouch for that. I’ll be sure to tell Nicholas that this year, there was someone extraordinary.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Krampus_Seasonal_G: Only those who are truly enjoying this winter’s festival can claim my Golden Bell. Bring me one, and I’ll give you a small gift in return.
Only those who are truly enjoying this winter’s festival can claim my Golden Bell. Five of them means you did more than just watch, so I’ll have a decent reward ready for you.
Only those who are truly enjoying this winter’s festival can claim my Golden Bell. Fifteen of them means you’ve completely taken over the festival, so you can expect something special.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Leathersmith_Compl: Ah, these are perfect and will be useful in other searches as well. Thank you. She’s as adventurous as they come. If you happen to hear anything, please let me know.
Accept these tokens of my thanks, and be sure to return soon—I have other tasks that could benefit from your skills.

Your efforts are deeply appreciated. Every day, I grow more weary, but I cannot give up hope. The woodsman has also tirelessly assisted me in this search, and I believe he harbors a special fondness for her. Thank you for persisting.
You found all of that in just 10 Oak Chests? With loot like that, I bet it wasn’t easy!
Ears and bones... Not quite what I had in mind when I said 'proof,' but I suppose they'll do!
You really went down there, and lived to tell the tale... I knew you were up for it. By the way... Did you hear anything unusual while you were down there?

You have my thanks. It is disappointing that nothing was found, but in a way it is also a relief. It must mean there is still hope. Even so, the passing of time takes its toll. I can only hope this worn body holds out until I find my daughter.
This blow will be noticed by the warlord himself... His presence weakens with every act of justice, bringing us closer to breaking his hold over the Crypts.

It is true! The souls are free, and his corrupted blade lies in pieces! This victory will echo in songs sung at the Tavern for generations! No reward could ever fully honor this deed, but I hope these weapons serve as a worthy start!

Thank you. With a bit of mending, these should do well enough. I only hope this helps keep those young ones a little safer. After all, there's nothing more important than returning home alive... to the ones waiting for you. You take care as well, adventurer. Do you understand?

It brings me true relief to see you return in one piece. I had faith in your skill, of course, but the worry... it never truly leaves me. Now that I’ve seen you safe, perhaps tonight, I might finally get a bit of sleep.

This... this was found there? No, no. This is not my daughter. It cannot be. It must not be. No... Please... I cannot believe it. I will not believe it. Please, leave me now. I... I must go to the alchemist. Perhaps he can tell me whose remains these truly are...

Thank you for what you’ve done. They won’t be thinking they can raid and plunder without consequence any longer. Still... it troubles me. I’ve never seen goblins act with such coordination before. This sort of behavior... it’s not like them. Not in the old days.
Truly remarkable. Your skill only seems to grow with time. You've more than earned a reward befitting your ability. I hope it pleases you.

The goblins I knew used to care for little more than food. They never fought to gather weapons or trinkets like they do now. It's strange... deeply so. I fear what might lie at the end of this unnatural behavior.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Leathersmith_Greet: Greetings, adventurer. I need leather caps—any type will do. They’ll be essential for keeping our fellow adventurers warm as they help with the search. Your assistance in gathering these would be greatly appreciated.

The Ruins have long been a place of both promise and peril. It reminds me of how much my daughter always fancied the statues in that forsaken place. My searches there have yielded little, but perhaps you might discover something new.

Good to see you again. Those old campsites in the Ruins were once places of respite for us. Travelers and trappers alike knew them well. Search these areas for any hints that might shed light on my daughter’s whereabouts.
I heard you can find all sorts of things inside Oak Chests scattered throughout The Frost Mountain... Would you mind opening a few for me?
The Frost Mountain is crawling with angry little Kobolds and animated Skeletons! If you can help clear the place up I might have something for you... also... bring back proof of your work.
There’s word of an Ice Abyss hidden deep with the depths of The Frost Mountain... Ice Hounds and Frost Sentinels are said to be a common sight down there... take a look for me, will ya?

The last place my daughter went was the Ruins. After all word of her was lost, I searched that place time and again but found nothing. Now I only hope to find even the smallest trace of her, even if it is found among the monsters that roam the Ruins.
Death’s lieutenants have corrupted every corner of The Forgotten Castle. Eliminating them will deliver an irreparable blow to their evil. This is just the beginning of cleansing our land.

You’ve proven yourself worthy of a task I once deemed unspeakable. The fallen warlord who haunts the Crypts with his deathly grip has revealed himself once more. I cannot say how much longer his presence will endure, now is the time to act!

Not long ago, a new band of adventurers passed through here. Did you happen to see them? Strangely enough, they were made up just like the group my daughter once traveled with... It brought back memories I hadn’t touched in years. I’d like to offer them a small kindness, if I may. They’re young still, and it shows in the state of their armor. If you could help me gather some gear and fabric, I would see it properly repaid.

The skeletons in the Forgotten Castle are always a trouble. Especially for the inexperienced, who often panic at their strange, jerking movements and end up badly hurt. I ask that you clear out some of those creatures, for the sake of the ones who have only just begun their journey. But even for someone as seasoned as you, carelessness can be dangerous. Please, adventurer... do not let yourself be harmed.

Last night, I had a dreadful dream. My daughter was crying out from deep within the Inferno. I was frozen in place, unable to move a single step, and all I could do was watch as she suffered in the distance. Adventurer, will you go to the Inferno on my behalf? There is something there, I am certain of it. Please, find it. Please, help put an end to my daughter's tears.

The goblins have taken to raiding the merchant caravans passing through these parts, and even the materials I purchased with what little coin I had have vanished in one of their attacks. I can't make sense of what’s driving them, nor do I have the strength to fight back myself, but we can't simply let this go. If you find any crates in their cave, break them. Smash every last one you see. They must be made to answer for what they've done.

The most dangerous creatures in the goblin cave are the cyclops and the troll. Folks have long hoped the two would turn on each other, but strangely enough, some sort of bond seems to have formed between them. Friendship between monsters... I can't understand it, and truth be told, I’d rather not. Take them both down, and bring back whatever spoils you find.

Ever since you shattered all the crates in their cave, the goblins have begun hoarding their loot in golden chests, or so I’ve heard. Their senseless raids haven’t stopped either. Adventurer, this time I ask you to target the golden chests. Take as many as you can.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_01_: You’ve returned safely. That is a relief. Seeing you come back unharmed gives me a small measure of hope.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_02_: It is truly a relief that nothing was found. The thought that they may still be alive somewhere has eased my heart. I can only hope that they have escaped the danger and found a safe place to hide.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_03_: ...So none of them returned with their senses intact. I had considered that possibility, yet hearing it spoken aloud weighs heavily on my heart... Still, this guilt is mine to bear as well.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_04_: Well done. They were once companions who shared in our quiet daily lives. It seems so much was lost because of our misguided choices.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_05_: I can hardly believe some of the bodies are already reduced to bone. It seems Ignir is corrupting everything in that place. We must stop him before it is too late.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_06_: You have done well. Thanks to you, Ignir’s influence has been pushed back, if only for a short while. But it will not last. He can always create new servants. We must now prepare for the next step.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_07_: The instability in the flow of fire is an important sign. It likely means that Ignir’s power is being spread thin as he expands his dominion. We must act quickly.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_08_: Well done. We have now made all the preparations we can. With those who aid Ignir lying low, we must not let this opportunity slip away. When you are ready, please come to me.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Complete_09_: This will not be the end. Spirits like Ignir do not fade so easily. He is likely hiding within the lava, waiting for another chance. Before he can regain his strength, I will seek a way to seal him completely. Thank you, truly, for all the help you have given us.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_01_: Through our misguided choices, the calamity of fire that lay dormant, Ignir, has awakened. I barely managed to escape that place, but many of my kin are still held there, bound by his control. To save them, I will need your help, Adventurer. But before I ask you to take on such danger, I must be certain that this is something you can endure.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_02_: When I fled my homeland, there were companions who escaped alongside me. But in the chaos of our flight, the bridge we were crossing collapsed, and we were scattered apart. Since then, I have heard nothing of them... Please investigate the site where the bridge fell. I hope it is not so, but if you discover anything, let me know.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_03_: Could you check on the condition of my kin. Ignir slowly eroded our minds, until he finally seized our will and forced us to labor for him alone. But if there is even one who still retains their senses, I do not wish to abandon them. Even if conflict arises in the process, it may simply be unavoidable.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_04_: Ignir has twisted not only my kin, but also the beasts of that land. They were once animals we raised, but now they wander through the flames, stripped of reason and driven to rage. If left unchecked, they will become a greater threat. Put them down and bring back what remains as proof.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_05_: Those who recently returned from my homeland say they found the bodies of our kin there. But when I escaped that place, they were still alive, though under control. I do not know what happened in the time between. Adventurer, please examine the condition of the fallen and report back to me.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_06_: My kin who have been enthralled continue to dig without rest. As a result, the lava fields have spread, and a lava golem has emerged. That golem is, for all intents and purposes, a thrall of Ignir. As Ignir’s influence grows, the golem’s strength will grow with it. We must bring that creature down before it is too late.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_07_: Before we confront Ignir, it would be wise to assess his current state. Please investigate the area around the great forge. Observe the condition of the flames and the flow of the lava, then report back. As Ignir is devoting his strength to expanding his control, he cannot be maintaining perfect command over everything. We must find that opening.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_08_: Fire spirits and elementals are beings that aid Ignir in restoring his strength. They act as conduits, gathering the power of fire and delivering it to him. If left alone, the scattered power will quickly come together again. To slow that process, even if only a little, we must eliminate them.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Miner_Greeting_09_: According to legend, a fully awakened Ignir is a being made solely of living lava. But due to the seal breaking incompletely, he now bears the form of a colossus, solid stone entwined with molten fire. We must stop him before he regains his true form. Adventurer, please put an end to him.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Navigator_Complete: This is good quality. With timber this sturdy, it shouldn’t break easily. I’ll begin repairs on the deck and hull with what you’ve brought. There’s still more work to be done, so I may ask for your help again soon.
The fabric is thick and sturdy. It should hold its own out on the sea. Just a bit more work and she’ll be ready. I can’t wait to see the sails catch the wind.

Thank you, adventurer. Thanks to you, my ship feels reborn. Guiding a strong vessel swiftly and safely is what I do best. I may well be the one who’s sailed near the Blue Maelstrom more than anyone alive. Now, at last, I can return to the sea.
You’ve done well. I can’t forget what happened that day, but it feels as though a small part of the debt has been repaid. Still, this is only the beginning. For now, I simply want to thank you.

There were all kinds of things inside. Likely remnants from sunken ships. In a way, I suppose you could call them keepsakes, traces of those who never made it back. Thank you for taking the time to look.

Thank you for accepting, even though it was no simple request. I swore I would do whatever it takes to avenge my fallen crew, no matter how difficult the path. And to do that, I need the help of someone like you. I’ll be counting on you from here on.

Well done. Thanks to you, our scouting efforts should go more smoothly for a while. All I can do now is hope they find my brother’s map. It was taken when he was captured by the pirates, so it must be somewhere in the Ship Graveyard.

This map is a keepsake filled with my brother’s passion. He was an archaeologist, and together we searched for signs of ancient ruins and forgotten sea routes. We once promised to set sail and explore them, should we ever find a promising lead. I intend to carry on that dream, even if I must do it alone. This map will be the beginning.

A fortress-like structure, you say? Then it must have been built by human hands. How intriguing. If my brother were still alive, he would have been thrilled by such a discovery. I'm only a navigator, so I can't say much more, but even I can tell this is something worth studying. I’ll try to find an archaeologist who might be interested. For my brother’s sake.
This... this is my crewmate’s journal. He was fond of keeping records, always curious, always jotting down everything he learned. I never thought I’d see this again. Thank you, adventurer. Truly.

The pearl truly holds a glow within it. And the coral... it's thicker, with a strange texture unlike any I’ve seen. I only wish he could have seen them himself. I’ll deliver these to his family, along with the journal he left behind.

My ancient compass points to places connected to the item placed upon it. If we set the Crocodilian eye here, it should respond... Hmm. It’s pointing to a land abandoned long ago. I’ve heard the river there dried up, the earth turned foul, and nothing lives there now. This warrants investigation.

Thank you for checking. It seems their weapons aren’t in as good a condition as I feared, and they don’t appear to be hiding much either. What I need now is someone with the skill to surpass them. Someone like you, adventurer.
Well done. They seemed unstoppable, and yet... here we are. Victory, at last. Now, only one step remains. Adventurer, I need your strength one final time.
It’s truly over. I hope this means my fallen crewmates can finally rest in peace. And as for me... perhaps it’s time I started living for myself. Thank you, truly.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Navigator_Greeting: Well met, adventurer. Might I ask for your aid in repairing this old ship? With a bit of work, she could sail again as a proper merchant vessel. Should you choose to help, you’ll be fairly rewarded. For now, I’ll need stout timber, strong enough to hold against the sea’s fury.

I bought this ship with the coin I earned working as a merchant navigator. I would have liked a better vessel, but this is what I could afford. Sometimes, you simply make do with what you have. Now I need a new sail. If the fabric is weak, it won’t catch the wind properly. Please bring me sturdy cloth and a set of sewing tools.

Once you’ve been aboard a ship, you’ll come to see just how many ropes are used throughout. They wear down quickly, and constant maintenance is a part of life at sea. Bring me several ropes. It’s all right if some are worn. I can trim away the bad sections and salvage the rest. As long as the critical lines are secured, we’ll be ready to depart.

The pirates roaming the Ship Graveyard belong to the infamous Black Despair crew. They’ve plundered countless vessels and left a trail of death behind them. They're the reason I walked away from my life as a merchant navigator. I cannot forgive them. Adventurer, I ask you to see that they are dealt with.

Have you seen the large, shell-like structures scattered across the Ship Graveyard? Among sailors, they’re known as mermaid coffins, though no one truly knows what lies within. My brother once studied them. It doesn’t matter much anymore, but still... I’d like to know the truth, if only for his sake. Please, take a look inside one of those coffins.

Each of us has our strengths. I know how to command a ship, but I'm no fighter. That is why I’ve been searching for someone who could stand in my place, someone skilled in both battle and survival. Someone who could help me see my revenge through. Adventurer, will you show me what you’re capable of?

The Tidewalkers are a troublesome foe. Once they spot an enemy, they attack without hesitation, no matter the circumstance. They're especially aggressive when accompanied by one of their shamans, so caution is advised. A scouting party I sent out recently has run into serious trouble because of them. I could use your help. Subdue them, if you can.

During the last search, we were fortunate enough to recover a portion of the map I’ve been looking for. But it isn’t enough. We need the remaining pieces. With both the monsters and the pirates still prowling that place, continuing the search is proving too difficult. Adventurer, would you help me recover the rest of the map? I’m asking for your help.

Adventurer, I have a favor to ask. While examining my brother’s map, I found a marked location deeper within the Ship Graveyard. It’s labeled for investigation, though I don’t know what he hoped to find there. Could you look into it for me? If anything stands out, please let me know.

When my ship was taken by pirates... I was lucky to survive, but the others weren’t. Most were thrown into the sea, and that was the last I saw of them. The waters near the Blue Maelstrom are full of man-eating fish. Adventurer, please deal with them. And if you find any items that might have belonged to sailors, bring them to me. I want to know if they were people I once knew.

While reading through my crewmate’s journal, I found something interesting. It speaks of glowing pearls and unusually shaped coral near the Blue Maelstrom. It seems he truly wished to see them with his own eyes. Adventurer, would you help me find them? I’d like to fulfill his wish, even if it’s a little late.

My brother’s research notes speak of a great river that once existed and a guardian said to dwell within it. Most of it is speculation, but the description of the guardian is hard to ignore. A beast with massive jaws, a vertical eye, and thick, leathery skin... It might be connected to the Crocodilian. Hunt them down and bring me one of their eyes. There’s something I need to confirm.

We’ve scouted much of the Ship Graveyard, but the area where the pirates gather is beyond what our search parties can handle. Adventurer, I need you to investigate the places they frequent. We must know what kind of weapons they’re hiding and whether they’re preparing for something. They’re not to be underestimated, so be careful.
The Black Despair pirates are blindly loyal to their captain. They’ve long claimed dominion over these seas, plundering and burning countless ships. Now it’s time they were repaid in kind.

There isn’t a sailor alive who hasn’t heard of Captain Bladehand. That wretched pirate has long been a scar buried deep within me. Ever since the day I survived his attack, I’ve waited for the chance to take revenge. Now, everything is in place. Adventurer, I ask you to end him.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Navigator_Title_02: The Cloth That Wraps the Wind
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_NightmareMummy_Com: There were no clear signs, I see... but it matters not... While I waited for your return... a memory came to me... I was there, in that castle... I remember writing something... and watching someone die... so many... so many deaths...
You say they were all mindless monsters... No... they were not monsters... They too were once living people... What led them to death... was magic... my magic... our magic... Ah... I have sinned...!

No... it wasn’t that... What I seek is not treasure... It was... yes, something terrible... something written down... Ah... my head... it feels as if it will shatter... This pain, it’s too much... I cannot think... Please... make it stop... make it stop...

Yes... this is it... At last, all has returned to me... Adventurer, I was a sorcerer of the castle... The experiments were ordered by the court mage... I believed it was a work to preserve life... but the truth was far darker... When I learned what it truly was, I tried to destroy the scroll... but I failed... and I too became one of the subjects... Now that I have it again, I can finally put it to rest... and perhaps, at last, find peace... Thank you, adventurer...
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_NightmareMummy_Gre: I remember not who I am... what deeds I once performed... nor even the reason for my death... There is but one thing I recall... that I am searching for something... That yearning alone stirred me from my slumber... Perhaps, if the coffins within the catacombs were opened... some trace may yet remain... Adventurer... would you help me recover the memories I have lost...?

Adventurer... I ask thee to journey to the place where others like me have begun to stir... Seek out any among them who, like myself, may have recovered fragments of their memory... If such a one exists, you may be able to speak with them... and perhaps then I shall learn what it is I am truly seeking...

...What is it that I so desperately longed for... Was it treasure... or jewels... such things as these... Could it be that mere filthy greed... was what led so many to their deaths by my hand... Gods, let it not be so... Adventurer... bring me the gems... If I see them with my own eyes, perhaps I shall know the truth...

At last, I remember... What I seek is a scroll... one that holds knowledge most dangerous... It was used to draw out the essence of darkness... using people... leading them, in the end, to death... That scroll is unlike any other... it has not faded, nor has it decayed... and it still lies somewhere within the castle... Adventurer, I beg you... please, find it for me...
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_NightmareMummy_Tit: The Scroll That Should Not Be
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_SkeletonFootman_Co: While we're on the subject of bones, I've amusedly listened to countless theories about our bleeding—from magical explanations to scientific fantasies. But between us? I suspect the powers that control our world simply find it visually appealing, delightfully grim.
You've survived! That’s more than most of my acquaintances can say.

Good! Very good. Our skeletons will come back stronger, after some properly bone-deep training. And it's all thanks to you. If anything else comes up, we'll handle it next year. For now, let's enjoy the celebration.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_SkeletonFootman_Gr: Greetings, adventurer. I’ve got a bone to pick with you. Your constant skirmishes have left some of my companions somewhat disassembled. After enduring a year of relentless battles, I'm taking a well-deserved break and seeking a capable adventurer like you to aid us.
Ever wonder what a skeleton's day job is like? Try surviving these places. It's not all rattling bones and eerie moans. Try surviving where we reign; it might just chill your marrow.

Lately, I've heard whispers that my comrades are falling far too easily. As proud skeletons, we must show we're not just hollow-boned fools. Bring me their skulls. As many as you can. I'll make sure the lesson sticks.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_01: Thank you so much! The truth is... I'm an orphan. If my uncle hadn't taken me in, I don't know where I'd be now. I'm truly grateful for everything he's done, I really am. But... sometimes I think he's a bit overprotective. Still, I suppose it's up to me to prove myself first. If I can do that, then even he won't be able to say no.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_02: Oh no... So most of the statues are broken? That's really sad to hear. Just imagining them shattered like that... it makes my heart ache a little. I wish we could bring some of the pieces back. But I suppose that would be difficult, wouldn't it? They're probably far too heavy... What a shame.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_03: I've never met someone as kind as you, adventurer. Especially someone who actually listens to what I say, instead of just brushing it off. I'll do my best from now on to be of real help to you, too!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_04: Thank you so much! I think I may have taken it all too lightly. I really believed I could handle it on my own... but now I see I wasn't ready. Next time, I’m going to try finding a companion or two. If we go together, maybe we’ll make it farther than just the entrance.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_05: Wow, the ceiling's really that high? I can hardly imagine it! And if there's even a bridge inside... it must be huge! The whole floor made of ice too? I’d probably slip the moment I stepped in. Still... I’ve made up my mind! My next adventure will be to Frost Mountain! I want to see it all with my own eyes!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_06: I’m so sick of skeletons now. I don’t ever want to see those creaky, clattering things again... Thank you, adventurer. I think I can finally get a good night’s sleep with both eyes closed. From now on, you can leave all your preparations to me. I’ll make sure everything is packed just right, extra carefully, just for you!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_07: Such a wonderful gift... There is no one else like you in the whole world, adventurer. Thank you, truly, thank you. I promise, this time I will not break it or lose it. I will treasure it with all my heart, I swear. And I will not give up until I become a real adventurer.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_08: Hearing your words makes me feel a little more at ease. I’ll be careful and stick to the places you mentioned. I promise! So, wish me luck, alright?
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Complete_09: I’ll never forget your kindness. I won’t give up until I truly become an adventurer, no matter what. And I’ll keep doing my best to help the other adventurers too. Especially you. I’ll make sure everything is prepared with extra care, just for you. Thank you so much!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_01: Hello, adventurer. Um... could I ask you for a small favor? I'm helping out adventurers here for now, but it's always been my dream to go on a real adventure myself someday. My uncle, the Tavern Master, keeps saying it's too soon and won't let me go. But I just know I could do well, if I had some decent gear. If you could find me a few pieces... would you, maybe? Please?
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_02: I know it's just a Ruins now, but it used to be a grand castle, didn't it? It's become a lair for monsters these days... but I've heard that many of the old statues are still standing, hidden throughout the place. I was wondering... could you look for them in my stead? I'm not quite ready to go there myself, not yet. Please... would you do that for me?
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_03: They say the Forgotten Castle is haunted by skeletons that walk on their own. What kind of terrible curse could force them to rise, even in death, never knowing rest? Whenever I talk like this, people tell me not to dwell on such things... but I can't help it. I think it's all so very sad. Please, adventurer, help those poor souls find peace.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_04: I went to the Forgotten Castle on my own not long ago... but I barely made it past the entrance before some beast started chasing me. I ran for my life and somehow got away, but I lost my weapon and my armor’s all torn to bits. Becoming an adventurer... it’s not quite how I imagined. I’d go back and try again, but I don’t have anything to wear or wield anymore. Adventurer, could you help me find new gear? Something a little better this time... please?
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_05: Adventurer, have you ever been to Frost Mountain? Just imagining a place where it's always winter feels like something out of a dream. Especially the ice caves. I'm sure they're filled with crystal-clear ice, glittering like gemstones. And the ceiling must be lined with huge icicles, hanging down like frozen spears. It must be such a breathtaking sight! If you ever go there, would you tell me what it was like? If anything stands out, something truly magical, please promise you'll share it with me!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_06: Adventurer... the skeletons were nothing like I imagined. I thought I would feel sorry for them, but I didn’t. They were terrifying. I only saw them from afar, but I was so scared I couldn’t even move. And the ones in Frost Mountain were even worse. Their bones were all frozen blue, like they had been trapped in ice for ages. It was awful. Please, adventurer, can you take care of them? I don’t think I’ll be able to sleep until they're gone.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_07: The Frost Mountain adventure was a complete disaster. I barely made it out alive, and only thanks to the companions who were with me. I lost all my gear too... the ones you worked so hard to find for me. I'm such a fool... You don’t have to say anything to comfort me. My uncle was right. Maybe someone like me just isn’t meant to be an adventurer... What? You want to help me get new equipment again? No, please, don’t trouble yourself because of me. Adventurer? Adventurer, wait!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_08: This time, I don't want to be a burden to anyone, so I'm looking for a place I can explore on my own. I heard the Goblin Caves aren't too difficult for a beginner adventurer. What do you think? Still, the thought of going alone is a bit scary... If you don’t mind, could you check the caves out first? Just to see if there are any safe spots or places to hide, even just a little. Hehe... thank you.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_09: Well... I did make it as far as the cave entrance, but... there were a lot more goblins than I expected. With that many, I don't think I could handle even one on my own. And if they surround me, I’d be in real trouble. Adventurer, would you be willing to take care of some of the goblins for me? I think I’d find the courage to try again if I knew it was a little safer.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Surgeon_Complete_0: While you were gone, I confirmed my hypothesis. They’re not healing like they should, and I can’t help but wonder if whatever was used to make those cuts was coated in some kind of poison. I need to look into something, and I’ll need your help soon, so hurry back.

As I have grown older, my knowledge has increased, yet there is still much left to learn in this world. The entities found in the Ruins are among them. It is time for a more thorough examination of things whose nature remains unknown.
What you found in those chambers paints a clearer picture, but there’s still much to unravel. The ritual is tied to the curse, and we’re getting closer to understanding its source.
Great job! Just what the doctor ordered!
Simply incredible. Not in a millennia would I have ever guessed this to be the case. Do not disclose my actions to my brother as he despises my methods. Take these for your vow of silence.
That will do the job. Precision and reliability are important in my field of work. It’s a shame my brother doesn’t hold the same standards.
I hate to admit it but my brother’s concoctions may have some use after all. Still, I stand by methods as the most effective.
I must admit I was a little mistaken. It seems that the gods are more powerful than I initially thought.
I much appreciate your intrepidness. Your deeds are making valuable contributions to the advancements of knowledge.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Surgeon_Complete_1: Amazing isn’t it? There must be some antiseptic properties I should investigate.
Well done, my friend! I am happy to see that my teachings were able to keep you in one piece.
Amazing job! Keep exploring, keep learning, and who knows what other secrets you might uncover.

How was it? Did your condition worsen in any way? Or were there any side effects...? Are you saying it was truly fine? Even though the most basic hygiene must have been lacking, it still worked? ...If it’s effective, I suppose I can’t stop people from using it. Though I still hope they reconsider. In any case, thank you for letting me know.

Are you saying you heard nothing at all? ...I see. Very well. I asked you to investigate just in case, but perhaps finding nothing is actually for the best. At the very least, I hope the leathersmith never hears of these rumors. I don’t wish to see that look of disappointment on his face again.

Thanks to you, I’ll have enough materials to experiment with for a while. I only hope that at least one of these fabrics proves useful as a resource. First, I’ll need to boil them thoroughly to cleanse them.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Surgeon_Greeting_0: I’ve had an influx of patients recently—so I need more supplies, stat. Many of them have those marks, carved deep into their skin. Some of the cuts are precise, almost surgical, while others look like they were made by a less experienced hand. There’s something about these wounds that’s disturbing.

I am a physician, but there are things in this world that cannot be treated with a scalpel. Curses, souls, and other abnormalities. Such entities exist even within the Ruins. They do not behave like anything that truly lives. I cannot heal them, but I can study them.

I’ve been investigating the Spectral Knight’s chambers, and I’ve found signs of recent activity. Something happened there recently, and I need you to search for traces of a ritual. It’s vital we uncover what was done, as it could give us a clearer understanding of what we’re up against.
Oh dear, it looks like our medical supplies are running dangerously low. You’ll be able to retrieve more from the crates hidden in the Forgotten Castle.

I must admit my curiosity for knowledge gets the best of me at times. I’m interested with the inner workings of a couple particular creatures in the castle. Your assistance in this matter would be greatly appreciated.
Surgery is a delicate art that requires the proper tools. Although my current supplies are adequate I would be more comfortable with a few more at hand.

Suffering an unattended injury in the unforgiving chill of the mountains can be a death call. I can explain the process but I recommend first hand practice with proper first aid to improve your survival odds. Only utilize a potion if worse comes to worse.
Even as a man of science, I must admit that the power of the divine have their role. I am however curious as to the limits of the gods. I have a simple experiment I’d like you to undertake for me.
I have an odd request of you. I’m very interested in the anatomy of our giant cousins. If you could bring me a few of their toes for research, I’d be extremely grateful.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Surgeon_Greeting_1: I’ve discovered a powerful use for maggots and mold to help heal the body. If you don’t believe me here is what you need to do.
I fear that the forces of darkness grow ever stronger. You must be our beacon of hope and if you should ever be injured in battle, remember what I have taught you.
Alas, I have a final task to ask of you. There’s a door, marked by stone or bones. Beyond this door is an ancient evil who must be vanquished.

More and more people are using the medical supplies found in the dungeon. I warned them not to use unverified items, but no one seems to listen. Do you think the same way they do? ...Adventurers, honestly. If that’s the case, then at the very least, I want to ensure their safety. Please help me by testing as many of these dungeon-sourced medical supplies as possible and reporting the results.

Strange rumors have been spreading recently. They say screams can be heard throughout the Forgotten Castle. Of course, that place has never been silent—I know that well. However... they claim these are the screams of a woman. Yet, there were no female adventurers present. Could you verify whether this is merely a rumor or something real?

I am considering ways to repurpose the fabrics recovered from the dungeon. Since many adventurers are already using dungeon-sourced medical supplies without hesitation, I wonder if other materials could also be of use. If I find something suitable, it could help compensate for the shortage of resources. I would appreciate it if you could gather as many different types of fabric as possible.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_01: You haven’t lost your touch, it seems. But don’t think we’re done yet. This is only the beginning of something bigger, something far more intricate. We’ll move on to the next phase soon enough. When you’re ready, come back and we’ll continue this work.

Hmm, this fabric is thick and coarse. It wouldn’t be suitable for proper clothing as it is. I’d need a heavy needle and thick thread just to sew it. Still, the fact that it’s waterproof is quite appealing. I’ll need to give some thought to how I can make use of this tar.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_02: So it was those things that are neither dead nor alive. Where do these cursed creatures even come from? I have also heard of people returning from their expeditions in a rather peculiar state. I cannot help but wonder if there is a connection. This is something I must look into.
Well done. It couldn’t have been easy to keep it in such good condition. Thanks to you, I’ll be able to run a few tests with it. I’ll be counting on you again next time.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_03: Well done. The clues are there, but I can see this curse isn’t as simple as I thought. The deeper we go, the more complicated it becomes. Perhaps we should consult another merchant I know who has more experience with this.

This liquid is truly fascinating. It gives off a soft glow during the day and shines even brighter at night. Even the way it feels on my fingertips is something special. I’ll probably lose sleep for days just thinking about how and where to use it. Thank you so much!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_04: Good work, but you look like you’ve had your share of the wilds. This curse—it’s not just an accident of nature. There’s something behind it, something that keeps tightening the noose around us.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_05: Better, much better. You’re not quite the mess you were, but we’re far from done. Now, back to the task at hand. I need to have a word with someone. Meet me here later when you’re ready to continue.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_06: Ah, with these materials, I can work wonders. Let me weave my magic. There, now you look like someone I wouldn't mind being seen with.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_07: The bitter cold of Frost Mountain invokes memories of a time when my survival seemed uncertain. Yet here I stand, fabulous as ever! Now, onto matters of utmost importance - securing my status at the upcoming elite soirée. Be on your way so I can focus on what I am going to wear.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_08: Exemplary as always! I've worked hard to reach where I am, and I refuse to rely on any more handouts from my adopted family. So, lend your strength to make these lands safer, ensuring the wealthy continue investing here.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_09: Kudos acquiring the materials. You won't be the one making the offering, for they will know you are an imposter. I have someone in mind whom I will disguise as a potential Dark Follower to carry out this delicate task.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_10: Alright. I’ll make sure to deliver your brave tale—embellished just enough to suit the young lord’s taste. What is routine for us is nothing more than a fantastical story for them.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_11: Oh, there are a few things worth using. With a bit of embellishment, they should make for a fine tale. Thank you. But... I couldn’t help but notice, just like last time—you’re not exactly gifted at storytelling.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_12: Alright, this is graphic enough—disgustingly so. Now, let’s string it together and wrap it up nicely... Oh, don’t worry too much. I’ll only show just enough. Hopefully, this will make the young lord abandon his foolish dream.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_13: Well, you may not be much of a talker, but your sketches are surprisingly decent. Thank you. They’ll be quite helpful for my next design.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_14: Thank you. Your talents truly shine brightest as an adventurer. Thanks to you, Frost Mountain should be safe for a while. I’ll be able to visit with peace of mind now.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_15: Oh, you really did bring everything you could, didn’t you... First of all, these entrails, the stench is absolutely unbearable. I need to get rid of them before the smell clings to my fabrics. Now, the rest... intriguing, really. The horns have a magnificent curve to them. And this heart, how extraordinary. Cold as carved ice, yet still faintly pulsing. I like it. Get ready. I’m going to create something the world has never seen.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_01: You’ve arrived. Good to see you still standing. I’ve got a dark muse whispering in my ear and a new creation that demands to be brought to life. I need someone I can rely on for this task. Let’s make sure you haven’t grown lazy and soft like the cushions on my settee. We’re not getting any younger, unfortunately.

I heard the news. So it's finally possible to reach the Blue Maelstrom, is it? Perfect timing, really. I've been in need of new materials. Sailors, I’m told, coat cloth with tar to make it waterproof. Could you bring me a sail and some tar? The condition of the sail doesn’t matter. I simply want to examine the texture myself. I’m counting on you.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_02: Lately, I have been repairing more garments than making new ones, especially those worn by adventurers returning from their journeys. If they are damaged to this extent, the cause cannot be ordinary. If you are willing, could you look into it for me? Should you encounter anything dangerous, please take care and bring back anything that might serve as a clue.

Ink is hard to come by, which is why it's usually reserved for fine writing inks. But who’s to say the ink of a cuttlefish from the Blue Maelstrom isn’t something entirely different? If it can be used as a dye, this could be a remarkable discovery.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_03: Those survivors, marked and broken, are living in a nightmare far worse than death. Their suffering, bound by a curse, will not cease until we uncover the truth. The Inferno holds the key. There’s evidence of sacrifice hidden within its walls, and it’s up to you to find it. We need to understand who or what we’re truly dealing with.

I’ve heard rumors of jellyfish in the Blue Maelstrom that give off their own light. They say you can extract a glowing fluid from them if you manage to kill one. Could you get some for me? If I can use that fluid to create luminous fabric, I’ll have the attention and admiration of the upper class in no time!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_04: I’ve worked with fabric all my life, weaving threads into something stronger. But now? Now the threads of this land are fraying, unraveling. These creatures, this cursed wilderness—there’s something far darker at play here, and it’s not just about survival. It’s about control. They’re being manipulated. If we can cut down the monsters and uncover what they’re hiding, we might be able to stop the unraveling.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_05: Look at you, not quite as tattered as when you first came in, but still showing signs of wear. Don’t ignore it—those ruins don’t just take their toll on your body, they gnaw at your spirit, too. The Shrines of Health should do the trick for now, but you’ve got to keep yourself in one piece if you want to keep moving forward.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_06: Seeing you in this state takes me back to my own beginnings—digging through trash for scraps, with nothing to my name but hunger and desperation. Let’s gather what’s needed, and I’ll help you craft something that leads to a better tomorrow.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_07: Frost Mountain offers more than just cold winds and icy peaks. It holds the promise of timeless beauty, its wintry embrace offering a chance to defy the ravages of time.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_08: Amidst the opulent festivities of high society, I caught wind of troubling news. The rumors of some strange monstrous beasts roaming these lands. You know how most nobility are, don't you? They'll vanish to their countryside estates if we don't address this threat swiftly.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_09: We have an intriguing assignment today. You will be procuring materials so I can craft accessories as part of a covert operation, designed to deceive one of the dark lords. By gaining their favor, we aim to secure access and gather information.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_10: To win the favor of the upper class, one must know plenty of entertaining stories. Young lords, in particular, are especially fond of tales of adventure. One such curious young master has made a rather troublesome request—he wants someone to slay the monsters of Frost Mountain on his behalf and then recount the adventure to him. What do you think? Are you interested? At the very least, the reward will be generous.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_11: Hmm, it seems your tale was well received. This time, the young lord wants to hear about the fascinating locations in Frost Mountain. There’s only so much I can make up on my own, you know. Since we’ve already started this, why don’t you help me out?
