Explore Frost Mountain thoroughly and find places that are grand, beautiful, or unique enough to make for a good story.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_12: There’s a problem. The young lord enjoyed our stories too much—so much that he now insists on becoming an adventurer! His mother, the lady of the house, is furious! If this keeps up, my connections will be ruined! No, that cannot happen. It’s time to show this naïve young lord a taste of reality.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_13: Frost Mountain truly boasts a breathtaking view. I visited once, long ago, and the Ice Caverns in particular... such mystique, such atmosphere. It stirs the creative fire in artists like myself. Hmm, do you happen to know how to draw? If so, be a dear and sketch the caverns for me, will you? I have a feeling they'll spark some marvelous ideas for my next line.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_14: Looking at your sketches has only confirmed it for me, I simply must see it with my own eyes. But as much as my stitching is impeccable, I must admit, combat isn't exactly my forte. I know it's dangerous, and I’m not foolish enough to charge in unprepared. So how about this, you go on ahead and deal with the monsters for me. I promise the reward will be well worth your while.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_15: When I visited Frost Mountain, I caught sight of a wendigo in the distance. I used to think all monsters were just hideous brutes, but the wendigo... there’s something different about it. Striking. That peculiar form of its... it might even inspire some patterns or embellishments for a new outfit. Of course, I can’t very well ask you to bring one back alive, so just collect whatever parts you can find. I’ll decide later whether they’re worth using.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Title_11_EA: Tales of the Frost Mountain Expedition
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TavernMaster_Compl: When you put them down, did you feel it? A shift in the air, like something heavy finally lifted? I’ve got a hunch about it. You should pay a visit to the Fortune Teller—tell her I sent you. She might have more insight into what’s really going on here. I’ll be heading to see her myself soon enough... I’ve got a feeling in my gut, and it’s not the ale.

I’ve taken a look at what you brought back, and there doesn’t seem to be anything wrong with it. It smells fine, and it even seems fit to eat. All the more strange. What kind of magic could be at work in that cursed castle...

This map... it’s got history. Every mark on it tells of a time before everything fell apart. Maybe one day, I’ll tell you all about it over a drink... or perhaps over something stronger. But for now, the map is yours.
You’ve done well, but don’t relax just yet. There’s a long road ahead, and the challenges will only grow harder. The tavern’s packed at the moment—swing by later when things settle.

Well done. Those mages won’t be casting their spells again, and the champion’s fallen, as expected. But don’t let your guard down just yet. Had a strange visitor the other night—he was covered in blood and wore a necklace with freshly cut, bloody fingers. When he saw me looking, he quickly covered himself with his cloak, ate, and left. We’ll talk more later; never know who’s listening.

Good to see you back. The wenches? Still laid up with something, and I’m starting to think it’s more than just food poisoning. Things have quieted down for now, so I’m thinking of paying the Surgeon another visit. Hopefully, he’s got something that’ll get them back on their feet—customers are a lot more satisfied when there are busty women to serve them.
I’ll make sure word gets around that you’re not someone to be trifled with. Come by for a drink sometime, you’ve earned more than just the coin.
Back already? You look frozen solid! Go thaw out by the fire while I fetch you something to warm you up from the inside—my own recipe.
The search party should be in safer hands now. Come on back and take a seat. I’ve got some hearty stew waiting for you—warm you up after all that cold. You’ve earned it.

We’ve learned what we can for now, but we can’t afford to stop here. The darkness is spreading, and we need more information to understand how to break this curse. Time is slipping away. One of my wenches... she’s gone. Choked on her own blood and bile. The others may not be far behind. We need to press on, gather more answers before it’s too late for them—before it’s too late for all of us.

The priest, who tried to help, is now infected. He’s become one of them, twisted beyond recognition. We had no choice but to put him down before he could do any more harm. This curse is something different from the one that has plagued those marked by the runes carved into their flesh. I can’t help but wonder—are they connected in some way? Regardless, your findings have given us a new lead, and that’s something we can work with.

The Lich’s involvement is undeniable—he was the king’s most trusted, and from the evidence you’ve gathered, it appears he played a much larger role in this curse than we ever imagined. Yet, there’s still a possibility that he, too, was merely a pawn, tricked into believing he held true power. We must dig deeper and uncover more, but we also need to focus on preparing for the battles ahead. Visit me soon, adventurer—I must inform the others of our findings, and we must plan our next move.
I tell ya, that feeling of spiritual clarity after receiving a good ol' blessing is hard to beat!
You’ve returned safely. Seeing this, I know you dealt with those fiends for certain. Your skill is truly remarkable. I celebrate your victory and grant you a reward worthy of it.
Tonight we celebrate! Let’s drink to your health and fortunes!
I feel much safer now that you’ve cleared out a bunch of their kind. Take a seat by the fire and take a well deserved rest.
I knew I could count on you. The Collector's debt is settled, and as promised, here's something for your trouble.
Bravo! You’ve conquered the Frost Mountain’s deadliest foes. Come, have a drink with me. I’ve prepared a brew that’s as legendary as your deeds.

I knew you’d pull it off. You’ve done a great job, truly. More than anything, I’m just glad you made it back in one piece. Come now, have a seat. Let me pour you a pint of the finest ale in all the realm. Once you've had a good swig, tell me your tale from the Inferno.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TavernMaster_Greet: Once, those skeletons were men—brave warriors, sworn to protect this kingdom. But the king’s lust for dark power twisted them, and they became pawns in a game much larger than themselves. Their souls were bound by a curse that would not let them rest. There’s a prophecy, though—one that speaks of a ‘chosen one,’ someone who will break the curse and put these souls to rest. I thought I might be that one once. I had the strength, the will... but something happened—something I’ll never speak of. It shattered that belief. This chosen one, though... they were meant to end the curse, to give peace to the restless dead. I’m not saying it’s you, but... what’s the harm in trying?

That old castle should hold nothing but rot, yet food and drink still turn up there. Fresh fruit, even meals that are still warm, are not something to brush aside. If you find anything like that in the castle, bring it to me. And whatever you do, do not try eating it yourself.

I seem to have misplaced something important, something more than just paper and ink... a map, to be exact. It once led me to places I preferred to forget, but now I need it. The forgotten castle might still hold the answers, or perhaps more nightmares. Think you can find it in that cursed place?

Ah, you’ve returned. I paid a visit to our friend, but we’ll need a few things before we can move forward. It’s the first of many trials, if you can call them that. Gather what’s needed, and we’ll see where this leads. If you succeed, we’ll talk about the next step—but let’s not get ahead of ourselves, eh? One thing at a time.

I’ve got another task for you, and it won’t be pretty. The mages—they’ll tear through your defenses if you’re not careful. As for the champion... well, if you make it back, you’ll understand why they call it that. Take them down, and we’ll have one less obstacle standing between us and the truth. Keep your head on straight—this one's going to test your patience.

Good to see you back in one piece. Things are a mess around here—my wenches have all come down with something, and I’m starting to think it’s not just the roasted rabbit from the other night. In times like this, it’s always smart to have a backup plan. You never know when you’ll need a quick exit.

Word around the tavern is that some frost-bitten creatures have been roaming the outskirts, freezing everything in their path. I’ve got an old friend who might know a way to deal with them, but he needs some muscle first. If you’re willing to brave the cold, I’ll see you’re compensated properly. Just don’t let those icy bastards catch you off guard.

Now that you've got some experience under your belt, I’ve got a task that’ll put your skills to the test. We need to check the escape routes—make sure they're clear and ready in case things go south. It's cold out there, though, so make sure you bundle up. Last thing I need is for you to catch a chill... or worse.

Ready to face some real danger? We’ve got frost-covered fiends lurking in the shadows of Frost Mountain. A search party’s heading up to look for that missing girl, and they could use some backup. I need you to help clear the way, make sure they’re not walking into a death trap.

Things have been shifting in the shadows lately, and I’m not the only one who’s noticed. More and more of the merchants have been pooling their resources, exchanging whispers in hushed corners, trying to make sense of what’s happening. The tavern—once brimming with chatter and laughter—is quieter now. It’s as if the life here is slowly being drained away. Even my wenches, bless them, have fallen ill with a strange sickness, one I can’t explain. Some say the darkness is coming from the Forgotten Castle. And if we don’t do something now, it will be too late. The brothers have suggested we investigate the undead filth lurking there, to see if we can learn how to break this curse before it spreads any further, before we harm the ones we love.

It was hard enough dealing with the death of one of my wenches, but things have taken a far darker turn. As they were preparing her body for burial, she came back—alive, or at least, not dead. But she wasn’t the same. She was twisted, wrong. Her eyes, lifeless but burning with something unnatural. She attacked anyone who came near, even tearing a chunk out of one of the priests. They had no choice but to sever her head and burn her to keep her from spreading whatever curse had claimed her. This... this is the nightmare we’re dealing with. We must continue looking into the origins of this curse and find a way to stop it. If we can’t reverse it, then we need to learn the most effective ways to end these horrors before they spread further.

The lead has brought us here, adventurer, but we must not act hastily. It’s better to proceed carefully and find solid evidence before drawing conclusions. The Lich was once the king’s most loyal court wizard, and from everything we’ve uncovered so far, it seems he may have had a much larger role in what is happening than we first suspected. If we can find proof of his involvement within the Forgotten Castle, we might finally understand the full scope of this curse. Your task is simple: search the castle, and bring back anything that proves the Lich’s hand in this darkness. Only then can we begin to make our next move.
The fact that you’re still in one piece tells me the god’s are looking out fer ya. Might be a good idea to show your appreciation and offer some blessings at the shrines.
Would it not be a waste to squander the blessings of the gods within a tavern? I know of some demons who are well deserving of divine retribution. Hunt them down and bring me the proof.

The number of monsters within the Forgotten Castle continues to grow. Many adventurers strive to cleanse that place, yet it seems impossible to drive away the darkness entirely... Still, we cannot abandon this fight. Their numbers must be thinned. Defeat them and show me proof of your deeds. It will not be easy, but I ask this of you.
The skeleton army has been wreaking havoc up on that snowy peak. Can you get a handle on them before they become an even greater threat?
I owe the Collector a debt but I can’t just leave the tavern. Can you collect the items for me and I’ll make it worth your while.

Demonic forces have made their abode deep within the heart of the frost mountain. To top it off they’ve captured a terrifying frost wyvern. Who knows that terrible plans they intend to use that beast for. We need to take them out before they can spring into action.

More demons have appeared deep within the Forgotten Castle. Ugly things, worse than anything we've seen before. And we still don’t even know what’s causing the plague. Things aren't looking good. If this keeps up, something far worse could be waiting for us. Adventurer, please. Put an end to those demons from the Inferno.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TavernMaster_Tuto_: Well done. You can tell at a glance whether someone is a prepared adventurer or just pretending by how they deal with the undead. You are the real thing.
I hope you found something worthwhile. Those who come back with decent loot usually return here for an ale. If you have a little coin to spare, why not have a drink yourself.
You made it back without injury. That is good to see. With this level of skill, I can trust you with proper contracts from here on.

Welcome. If you are looking for information or companions, you have come to the right place. This is where adventurers and rumors tend to gather. But information often comes with danger. I do not give work to just anyone. If you want a contract, show me what you can do.

There are more useful items in a dungeon than you might expect, including things you can obtain without having to fight every monster. If I were to offer one piece of advice, do not pass by the small chests in the old castle. Take a closer look, and you may find something better than you expected.

As you know, the old castle is a dangerous place. With a bit of luck, you might find valuable gear or coin. But none of it matters unless you make it back alive. Adventurer, explore the Forgotten Castle and return safely.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TheCollector_Compl: Fantastic. You’ve done well. Now, go ahead and rest up; I’m sure you’ve earned it. Come see me soon when you’re ready to continue. We’re not done yet.
These are just the pieces I needed. There’s still much more to gather, but go ahead and thaw out. When you're ready, come back for the next task. We’re far from finished.

Good. I will see that these are delivered properly. The Fortune Teller and I sometimes seek things that may seem a little peculiar to others. But I do not concern myself with what people say. We know exactly what it is we must do.

The true worth of an object shines only in the hands of one who can recognize it. This one is no different. Thanks to you, I have obtained it, and you shall have your rightful reward. You have done well.
Such curiosities! I wonder who could have built such vast structures. We’ll need to prepare an expedition in the future!
Quick quick! Don’t let anyone see you with those. Hand them over and off with you!
My my, you’ve proven your strength. I shouldn’t have underestimate you.

My word! Bound in ropes and sunk beneath the waves, you say? Remarkable. This could be compelling evidence that something from the merfolk legend truly happened. Were they truly sacrifices, just as the stories claim? Or is there another truth we’ve yet to uncover? Fascinating. That place certainly deserves a closer investigation.

Truly impressive. It's been some time since I've seen an adventurer of your skill. I hope you won't take offense. This wasn't meant as a test. But after watching so many missions end in bitter failure, I'm sure you can understand my caution. In any case, you've earned my trust now, and I intend to reward you accordingly.
Well done. Thanks to you, we’ll be able to continue our investigation without trouble for a while. Here, take this. I hope it serves as a reward worthy of your efforts.
You’re proving more and more valuable to me. I’ll be sure to call on you when I have another interesting deal.

These scales have such a strange and mesmerizing hue. And this tear, this translucent droplet-shaped crystal, expands my view once more despite all the gems I’ve collected over the years. It is truly a breathtaking beauty.
That’s pretty impressive. Those beasts weren’t pushovers. Hope these items make up for your time.
Hope you didn’t get a hangover. Here’s a few coin to help you recover.
Hmm, some of these are a bit bloody, but no worries, I'll have them cleaned up in no time.
Let’s see what secrets I can uncover with these artifacts. I’ll let you know if I discover anything. In the meantime, here have these items.
Hmm I’m starting to notice a pattern. I think a few more pieces and I’ll have unraveled their origin.
Ah ha! That bowl was the missing link! This is all very interesting. Hmmm... a land lost to the sea. I apologize. I’m getting ahead of myself.

Oh... this is truly of great worth. I cannot deny that not only your skill, but also your eye for rarity grows keener with each step. Since you have brought me such a treasure, I shall grant you something special in return. And should you uncover more marvels in your journey ahead, be sure to bring them to me.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TheCollector_Greet: As always, I’m after something valuable, but this land is plagued with these beasts—Frost Wolves. I need you to thin them out, clear the path, so I can get what I’m after without being interrupted by these vile creatures.

I’ve got a rather long list of curiosities I’m chasing, but let’s start with these two. They’re not much on their own, but I assure you, they’ll help further my collection. As soon as you gather them, I’ll task you with the next item.

I received a request from the Fortune Teller, but of course she asked for an item I passed on to another collector not long ago. I have a few favors to ask of her myself, and I would rather not lose her goodwill over something so trivial. I will need to acquire it again. Would you help me? It should not be too difficult to find.

Objects found within dungeons may seem common, yet they are never truly ordinary. At times, the essence of the land or its creatures seeps into them, transforming them into something entirely different. Of course, most may be discarded, but if even the slightest possibility lies within... is that not worth the attempt?
I’ve been hearing of a wonderous gadgetry up on the great peak out yonder. Might you do my bidding and have a look out there?
Don’t be taken aback for what I’m about to ask. I need some very peculiar things and you’re the only one I can trust.
I apologize for being so terse. I get a little antsy when working on my secret projects. Anyways, I have another task that can lead to riches. Start off by eradicating the undead in the mountains.

Long ago, the merfolk are said to have offered themselves as sacrifices to calm the fury of the sea after committing a great wrong. Most dismiss it as an old tale, but I do not. Did you know there were once far more merfolk than there are today? There must be a hidden truth behind it. I want you to find out whether a merfolk grave truly exists within the Blue Maelstrom.

This time, the task will be a bit more difficult. The yetis of Frost Mountain resemble apes, but they are far larger. Despite their massive size, they are incredibly swift and cunning. If you can bring that creature down, I’ll be willing to consider a new offer.

I assembled a team to investigate the Blue Maelstrom, but their progress is slower than a slug. They say the merfolk there attack without hesitation. And to make matters worse, even the ones thought to be dead have begun to move again. I need your help. Deal with those wretched things, would you?
What I’d give to have a trophy of those ferocious beasts up on the mountains. Get me what I need an I’ll make it worthwhile.

It’s well known that merfolk lure people with their enchanting songs. But what fascinates me more is the merfolk themselves. Their shimmering, iridescent scales and the crystals known as mermaid’s tears. The tears in particular are said to form at the very moment their breath leaves them, like a final scream. What do you say, adventurer? If you can bring these to me, I promise the reward will not disappoint.
Been getting reports of some terrible beasts up on the mountain harassing my kin. Can you do a favor and take them out?
Heard it’s getting pretty cold up in the peaks. Nothing warms the body like a few good ales and taking out skeletons.
I got another peculiar request. I need a few items that only come from the terrible creatures up on that frost mountain. Get them for me and I’ll be sure to make up for your time.
I’ve heard on good authority that some old relics are more than what they seem. If there’s one thing I can’t resist, it’s a good mystery.
Those pieces you brought were just the tip of the iceberg. It looks like the rarer relics hold similar secrets. Can you check some of the more valuable chests for similar relics?
I know this next list of items is a little strange, but trust me, I’m getting close to discovering the secret of the relics.

Adventurer, there are many like me who seek rare and elusive relics. Such a pursuit is no mere pastime, but a noble path of inquiry. Ancient legends, hidden treasures, remnants of the past, traces of monsters... anything will do. Bring me what is truly rare, and you shall be handsomely rewarded.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Treasurer_Complete: Impressive! These gleaming gems will do the trick. The Collector will be satisfied, and you’ve more than earned your compensation.

The evidence you uncovered paints a grim picture of what’s happening. The ritualistic marks, the suffering... But if the rumors are true, and someone or something is devouring their souls, I wonder... Come back soon. I need to look into something.

The wraith is gone, but sadly, no change in the living. I’ll need to do some research and figure out what our next move should be. Come back soon; we’ll need to plan more precisely and carefully than when I’m balancing the books.

One of the bodies did indeed bear markings similar to those we’ve encountered before—though they seem slightly different. This suggests a deeper, darker evolution of whatever is at play. We’re not done yet, though. I’ll need more time to piece these findings together. Come back soon.

Good work. This is a solid start, but it won’t be enough to clear all the debts left behind by the dead. We’ll need more, but at least we’re on the right path. For now, this will help begin the process of easing their suffering.

Good work. The families have asked me to express their gratitude. One even baked you a Chocolate Chip Muffin as a token of thanks. Unfortunately, I seem to have misplaced it... though I swear I didn’t eat it. In any case, the silver and other valuables you’ve brought will make a real difference.

The chalice you’ve brought back is undeniably foul, a palpable darkness clinging to it like a stain. But is it the one we need? I’ll send it to someone more skilled in these matters to confirm our findings. In the meantime, I’ve been informed of other pressing issues that will require your attention sooner rather than later.

The information you gathered was helpful to my contact and is leading us deeper into the mystery. We’re starting to piece things together, though there’s still much left to uncover. The truth is closer now, but it’s going to take time to fully understand the significance of what we’re dealing with. Return soon—the next step of this journey is just ahead.

The throne has revealed more than we expected—its markings tell a story of power, loss, and untold secrets. But this is only the beginning. What we’ve uncovered is just a piece of the puzzle, and I fear the answers we seek lie deeper within the Inferno. You’ve seen enough to know there’s more to be found, though the path forward remains unclear. There’s a door that awaits, one that has been sealed for far too long. Once you’re ready, we’ll need to face whatever lies beyond it.
I didn’t think you had it in you... you really do know your way around down there. Don’t go too far, I will be needing your skills again soon.
That chest held everything I imagined and more! If you find yourself a few more chests like that, you might become the richest adventurer in town!
I knew you would find it, but I didn’t expect you to be so quick! I hope this reward is fair compensation for your tremendous effort.
Excellent plundering! With each haul from the chests, your riches grow evermore.
You’ve truly found it! When I first sent you on this journey, I never believed the legends were real. Yet here you are, proving me wrong—and bringing a myth to life.
These are perfect! How did you manage to find bangles in this condition? You really have a knack for getting the good stuff.

I hope you found something of value. I trust in your skill, but I have seen far too many adventurers who relied solely on their abilities—only to never return. I wish to continue doing business with you, so always ensure you are well-prepared.

Was there nothing unusual? I see... Actually, I’ve heard that an Alchemist has been searching for something lately. As you know, Alchemists will do anything in the name of their experiments—whether for good or ill, it hardly matters to them. This time, he’s looking for a particular item, and I find that concerning... If I find out what exactly he seeks, I will let you know.

This seems to be the one. It’s a relief that you found it first. Please keep this matter a secret from the Alchemist. I know he has accomplished remarkable things and has helped many people, but I worry that one day, he may cross a line he cannot return from. I only hope that day never comes.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Treasurer_Greeting: The Collector’s luck ran out when he tangled with the Goblin Merchant. Now, his debt has become my burden, thanks to an old favor I owe him. I need your help to settle it—one gemmed ring and one necklace. Find them, and I’ll ensure you're compensated.

Greetings. I’ve been occupied with a few matters lately—settling the debts of those who’ve passed and informing their kin of the burdens left behind. It’s a task that doesn’t get easier with time. But what’s more unsettling is the way these poor souls have been treated. Branded, tortured like animals, only to waste away in silence until death claims them. One of my patrons has provided me with a lead. They believe they know where their loved one was found. I think we should investigate.

You’re back. Good. I’ve been mulling over something—rumors of creatures that devour souls. The wraiths are the first of many, I suspect. If we slay them, perhaps the souls trapped in this cycle will find rest. And if we’re lucky, those still living might snap out of whatever trance they’re in. It’s a long shot, but it’s a start.

Rumors suggest that the bodies within may have been among the first to be subjected to the same ritualistic torment as those more recent poor souls. Search for any clues—check if their tongues were severed or if strange markings are carved into their flesh. We can’t be sure until we investigate. If there’s any connection, we need to understand it before this spreads further.

I can't get over these poor souls, their families left to shoulder the weight of debts they never signed up for. It’s a cruel irony—those who’ve passed, leaving behind not just sorrow but financial ruin. The living kin are trapped, burdened by the aftermath of their loved ones’ affairs. I want to help free them from this, but to do so, we need to gather the necessary funds. Bring me 150 silver coins, and we can start easing their suffering.

Nice to see you again. The families are starting to feel the weight lift, and I’m hoping there’s something of real value hidden inside those Mimics. Whatever we find could go a long way in easing their suffering.

I’ve heard whispers—dark rumors—of a chalice, one used in the first rituals. It’s said to lie hidden in the Forgotten Castle, a relic of blood and shadows. I don’t need to tell you that it’s no ordinary artifact. It’s something far darker. Something that could give us the answers we desperately seek, or drag us deeper into this abyss. I need you to find it before it’s too late. The darkness is spreading, and we need to understand what secrets it holds before they consume us all.

There’s a definite darkness to the chalice you found. While it’s still being researched, I’ve been informed that there were many pieces used in the original ceremony, fragments we still don’t fully understand. My contact is still digging deeper, but it’s suggested that the answers to some of these missing pieces may lie within the King’s Treasure Room. However, we’ll need to clear out any undead protectors lingering there before we can get close to the truth. Once you’ve dealt with the threats inside, come see me. We may be closer than we think, but this task is far from over.

The Inferno holds many secrets, but there’s one we’re desperate to uncover. The fallen king’s throne lies deep within its fiery depths, and you’ve been chosen to find it. Your task is clear: locate the throne and examine it for any unusual markings, glyphs, or relics. Every detail could hold significance. The throne may contain clues about the ritual, or perhaps the king’s true fate. We need to understand what’s hidden within.
Deep below The Forgotten Castle lies an iron door sealed shut. It is known to be heavily guarded... but the reason why is still unknown. I need you to go find out what that reason might be.

Rumors of a grand chest filled with blessed riches have echoed around these parts for years... but after hearing some tavern talk, I am convinced I know where it sits. If you think you have what it takes, I will guide you on your way to open it once and for all!

You seem to have proven your ability to explore the more dangerous parts of that castle... Now, I need you to find a Ceremonial Dagger! However, only the finest of quality will be accepted into my collection. The deeper you go, the easier it will be to acquire such a thing.

As we prepare for the battles ahead, remember, it's not just your weapons and armor that need upgrading. Your coffers must grow as well! Let's make some financial gains to ensure we're prepared for the unexpected.
I have heard stories of a stone door deep below The Forgotten Castle... It is said to hold unimaginable legendary treasures, so, how does a hunt sound?

I have been searching for bangles... but not just any bangles. I need bangles of the highest quality, would you know where to find any? You might have some luck searching those piles of treasure in that haunted castle... but be careful, you won’t be the only one searching for these.

What do you believe ensures safety in an adventure? Skill, of course, is essential. But when skill levels are equal, what makes the difference? Superior equipment. Unfortunately, while decent gear is easy to find here, truly exceptional equipment is rare. In truth, many such treasures lie buried deep within the Forgotten Castle, hidden among hoards of riches. You should seek them out.

Do you remember the stone door you opened last time? Now that we know for certain that treasures lie beyond such doors, we must investigate the rumors of other sealed passages as well. Open them and see what lies beyond. And... if you come across any treasure that carries a strange aura, be sure to let me know.

I’ve discovered what the Alchemist is searching for—a cursed crown. No matter what is done to it, it remains unscathed, and the gemstone at its center glows even in complete darkness. Can you find it before he does? I do not know what curse it carries, but this time, the Alchemist must not be allowed to obtain it. I have a bad feeling about this.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Valentine_Daily_Co: We may not be able to stop the spreading plague all at once, but if everyone lends their strength as you have, it will buy us time to restore the balance of love. Please, take this rose. It once bloomed in darkness, but through purification, it has regained its true fragrance. A living testament that, with love, anything can be restored.
I know it wasn’t easy, but your courage will pave the way forward. Sometimes, love spreads through the most unexpected paths.
This is exactly what I needed to know. Our combined efforts are working. If we keep this up, love will surely prevail.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Valentine_Daily_Gr: The season of love has come... yet the air is still filled with death. Skeletons, goblins, kobolds... the plague is spreading to everything that moves. For now, ending those who carry it seems to be the only way to slow its spread. I sincerely ask for your help.
Even the strongest creatures are not immune to this plague. Many adventurers avoid the riskiest encounters, but someone must face them. If you lead the way, I will make sure the risk is worth it.
I have yet to measure the true extent of this rot. Search everywhere you can. We must continue to monitor the situation.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Valentine_Seasonal: It may not be a grand reward, but if you continue to help keep this plague at bay, I will find a way to offer you something better.
I know it was no easy task, but I hope this reward brings you some small comfort. As long as we do not give up, we will surely see this through.
You have taken the lead in restoring the balance of love through your efforts. You are truly a Bringer of Love. I hope this gift can repay you for all that you have done.

The Black Rose has become a symbol of resistance against this plague. Once steeped in darkness, it has now been fully purified, bearing a new kind of beauty and fragrance. Bring me one, and I will reward you for your effort.

You are clearly making a difference, Adventurer. As more people join you in purpose, we will be able to overcome this trial all the sooner. As a token of that journey, would you bring me three Black Roses?

There is no defeat for the power of love. If you can gather ten Black Roses, that alone will stand as a great sign of encouragement in this arduous fight. It may take time, but I ask that you see it through to the very end.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Comple: These weapons will work. With them, I can begin the real work, but there’s more to this story. My great-grandfather spoke of an ancient sword hidden in Frost Mountain—crafted by the Dwarves who taught him... Well need to investigate this soon, but let’s rest for now.

You’ve found it. This sword... it’s more than I expected. I can feel its power, but it’s not just a weapon—it’s tied to something darker... We”ll have to travel back to the swords resting place and unveil its tainted history. Maybe those forsaken frost spiders guarding it that have plagued my lineage for centuries will give us a clue.

They’re dead, but something isn’t right. I can feel the sword changing me, just like it did my great-grandfather...The whispers are growing louder. I’m not sure how much longer I can resist... But we can’t stop now. I’ll need more from you soon...
Your hands tell the story... so don’t bother telling it to me. Here, these might make it easier for you next time!
Wow... and here I was thinking how ridiculous that sounded. Those Ruins are getting more dangerous by the day.
You brought these a lot faster than I expected... I guess you were prepared. If you come back later I might be able to craft something special for you.

Molten lava cascading like a waterfall... Their forges must be boiling at unimaginable heat. Now I see why dwarven craftsmanship advanced so far. No matter the effort, there are limits to how hot a fire can burn. But the land they lived in already provided perfect conditions.
You might not have found anything legendary, but at least have these weapons for your trouble.

Well done. This is the first time I have seen an obsidian ore of this size. The dwarves must have refined their craft by working with many different minerals since long ago. For a craftsman like me, this is like a dream come true.
I know that was a lot of work, but here! Hopefully, this makes it worth your time.

Even though most of it has melted beyond recognition the condition of what remains intact is astonishing. This durability and smoothness... the dwarves are not called master craftsmen without reason. Yet I sense no unusual magic here. Then where exactly was the dagger I inherited made...
I knew you wouldn’t regret it! Just look at all the valuables you brought back... and you get to keep this gift from me!

Well done, adventurer. With those beasts cleared out, my trade routes are safe again, and we can finally get back on track. I have a feeling we’re closer to uncovering the truth than ever before. Hopefully, nothing else slows us down.
Excellent work. While my wife’s health remains unchanged, the presence of family has lifted my spirits. These items should help us make progress, and I’m grateful for your dedication.
Thank you. If this turns out as I envision, it will be a weapon unlike any other. When that time comes, I shall craft one for you.

These weapons look like the work of dwarves. They’re the kind of craftsmen who can forge fine weapons without ever needing to rely on magic. But I suppose that wasn’t enough for them. To go even further, they must’ve reached for forbidden techniques. That hunger to make something better... I think I understand it now.

Thanks to you, things should quiet down for a while. I appreciate it. Those creatures... they’re born of malice itself. No matter how many you cut down, they just keep coming, like vermin. Until we deal with the source, this fight won’t truly be over.

By the gods, you mean they actually appeared? I can't tell if that's a blessing or a curse. Still, the fact that you brought them down is news worth hearing. Thank you for risking yourself to uncover the truth.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Extra_: Thank you for your efforts. These are quite serviceable weapons. If I examine them carefully, I am sure I will learn something from them. Now, as promised, I will give you the weapon I forged. May it serve you well.
Well done. All of this will serve as the foundation for me to make better weapons. Here, I present a new piece I recently completed. May it be of service to you, adventurer.

Well done. Thanks to you I have gained much insight and was able to complete this weapon. For now, this is the best my craft can achieve, but I will continue to strive ceaselessly to create something more perfect. For I know that effort will never betray me.

You cannot hope to forge a fine weapon by relying on luck. It takes constant practice, much experience, and even failure to shape something greater. Studying weapons already completed is of great value as well. If you bring me a few good ones, I shall exchange them for a better piece of my own making.

Forging ordinary weapons is not particularly difficult. But producing an exceptional weapon is an entirely different matter. The strength and balance a fine weapon must possess can never be fully learned by study alone. So if you bring me weapons that are a step above the last batch, I will use them as the basis to craft an even finer piece.

Adventurer, the time has come to take on a new tier. Drawing on the experience I have amassed, I intend to forge a weapon surpassing anything I have made so far. To complete it properly I require your aid. If you would procure for me several rare weapons not easily obtained, I shall present to you the fruit of my labour.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Greeti: My great-grandfather was a master craftsman, but his greatest work—enchanted daggers—came at a cost. He learned forbidden Dwarven techniques, but they led him down a dark path. Now, I must finish what he started. Bring me two rare weapons, and I’ll use them to forge something that will surpass all before it.

Let me tell you more. My great-grandfather once ventured into Frost Mountain, drawn by tales of a sword of great power. It was said to be forged by the same Dwarves who taught him their craft. If this sword is real, it could be the key to completing his legacy—and mine. Find it, and I’ll finally understand what he couldn’t.

These spiders aren’t just creatures—they’re part of the curse that has followed my family for generations. My great-grandfather fought them, and it nearly destroyed him. Clear the way—kill three of them—and I can study the sword in peace. We’re too close now.
Stone tombs, and coffins... The Forgotten Castle has an abundance of them... I bet some of them have never even been opened, but you might have to fight to be the first. What do you say?
Some fool came into the Tavern last night speaking of “Living Statues” flying around the Ruins... I haven’t ever seen such a thing, but would you mind taking a look?
I am in urgent need of Gold Ingots... I don’t know how you are going to get them, but if you do I will make it worth your time!

I never imagined the dwarves’ ancient homeland would lie beneath the mountain range, connected to the Goblin Caves. There was a reason we could not find even the slightest trace, no matter how thoroughly we searched Frost Mountain. At last, we can investigate the proper place. Adventurer, please confirm the dwarves’ land.
That castle is filled with old pots, I once found a legendary Falchion inside one. Why not shatter a few and see what fortune awaits? It’s tradition around these parts.

Obsidian is so rare that it is usually traded only as expensive jewelry. But weapons forged from obsidian are said to be sharper than those made from any other material. If you can bring me a small amount of obsidian, I will try forging one myself.
Those pots might not have held what you’re looking for... but surely the chests scattered throughout the castle grounds will. Why don’t you open up a few and report back what you find?

My great-grandfather even learned his craft from the dwarves, yet now we cannot communicate with them at all... If that is the case, conflict seems inevitable. If I cannot ask them directly, then I would like to examine the tools they have made instead. Their condition does not matter, so please bring me as many as you can.

If you are willing to push the limits of your safety, I can make it worth your time! I just need you to open a few Golden Chests, they are plentiful inside The Forgotten Castle. By the way, you’ll need to bring lockpicks to open those chests!

Good timing. Unfortunately, we’ll have to put our side mission on hold. A surge in monsters is wreaking havoc, and I’m almost certain it’s tied to what we were investigating. It feels like something doesn’t want us getting any closer. Even my trade routes are overrun by these beasts, so the sooner you help me clear them out, the sooner we can get back on track.

Remember that list I mentioned earlier with the glowing bug parts? There are a few more items we need to gather: some rotten fluids, high quality weapons, and ten armor scraps. It’s not a pleasant task, but I know you can handle it.

I have been racking my brain lately, trying to forge a weapon with greater power. Yet with the materials I possess, I cannot bring my idea to life. There are a few things I require, rare and not easily found. Will you help me?

Adventurer, bring me a few weapons that are not easily found. My goal is to forge a blade that can pierce through anything. Though I am still far from completing such a work, I refuse to give up and continue my attempts. This time I intend to test materials that are dangerous to handle. I must study them closely and discover how they might be used.

I’ve heard rumors that new demons have begun to appear in the Inferno. They’re stronger, and they hunt adventurers with ruthless precision. It would be ideal to drive them back into the darkness before they fully settle in... but at the very least, we can’t just let them grow comfortable. Take them down. I believe if anyone can do it, it’s you.

The masters of the dungeon have grown more cunning. Those beasts have slithered into deeper shadows than ever before. Luckily, if you bring the right materials to the alchemist, he says he can craft something to draw them out. I trust his skill well enough, but I prefer certainty over guesswork. Take what he gives you, see if it truly summons those monsters, and if it does, make sure they don't walk away.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Title_: In Search of the Dwarven Land
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Woodsman_Complete_: Those supplies you gathered will keep us from being another casualty of the cold. I know this lesson all too well. There was a time, not long ago, when I lost some of my closest companions to the freezing winter. I wanted to bury them, to give them the peace they deserved, but the earth was locked in ice, cold as death itself. When I finally returned to bury them properly, their bodies had vanished.

Nice job. The path is clearer now, and those less prepared have a better shot at staying alive. It won’t be easy, but you’ve given them a damn good chance. I appreciate the help—stay sharp; we’ve still got a long way to go.

Well, I’ll be damned. She was right... I don’t know how, but it seems we’re on the right path. It’s a sliver of hope, but it’s enough for now. And between you and me, that fortune teller lady freaks me out—she eats bloody eyeballs and all sorts of strange things.

Well done. This should keep things under control for a while. But since we still don't know the source of those creatures, all we can do is clear them out from time to time. I’ll be counting on you again when the time comes.
You found some good usable pieces. Wood is heavy, so it is hard for me to carry much on my own. Thanks to you, my work will be much easier. Thank you.
Ew, that place sounds just as disgusting as I’d imagine. I’d suggest you take a bath to get some of that stench off you.
Your skills are impressive as always. Unfortunately your report seems to indicate that darkness has overtaken the castle.
I was a fool for ever doubting your skills. Here, take these items as a token of my apology.
By the gods! You’ve done it. I haven’t felt this calm in years. Unfortunately, I’m not sure how long this will last.
Ah, nothing more comforting than a crackling campfire amidst the chill of the frost.
Impressive! Those giants are renown for their strength and you made it look easy!
You've done good work here, but always remember—the mountain never rests.
A frost wyvern?! My dear, what could have compelled the demons to capture such a terrifying beast?
A fine job in thinning out the forces of evil.
Good job. I know that taking out those beasts were no easy task. I only hope we put a dent in the plans of the frost demons.

You truly heard nothing? Truly...? That can't be... Another lead, ending in nothing... Sometimes, it feels suffocating, unbearable. When I think of her, suffering even at this very moment... Haa... Haa... No, this won’t do. I need to rest. Please, leave me be for now.

Thank you. Traveling through the area has become much easier—at least for now. I hope to find what I’m looking for before those creatures swarm back again... Ah, it’s a book. According to the Alchemist, these books could aid his research. Wish me luck.
Thank you so much. I won’t forget your help. Now, I just need to bring this to the Alchemist, and I’ll receive a new potion. The effects? ...I’ll tell you about them later.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Woodsman_Greeting_: People think it’s the beasts that get you in this land, but it’s not. It’s the cold. The hunger. It gets into your skin, your bones, and slowly, you’re dead before you even know it. I’ve seen too many inexperienced fools wander into the wilderness, too proud to listen to warnings, and they end up like the others. No one dies in their sleep out here unless they’re already dead. If you’re not careful, hunger and frost will do their work long before the claws of any creature ever get the chance. So it’s important to always cover your basics before any adventure.

A lot of people are helping in the search for the Leathersmith's lost daughter, but not all of them are as capable as you. There’s plenty of inexperienced souls stumbling into the wilderness, thinking they can handle it. It’s up to us to clear the path and make it safer for those who don't have the skills. We don’t want them getting in the way or becoming another burden.

Glad to see you made it back in one piece. The search for the Leathersmith’s daughter has turned up nothing, but I’ve been digging around... got desperate enough to visit that damn fortune teller. She gave me a place to check—let's see if there's any truth to her cryptic ramblings.

It seems the insects of the Inferno have evolved into something even more vile. The demon flies are said to explode in front of their chosen target, dealing harm in the blast. Truly revolting creatures. We must deal with these filthy pests before they spread any further.

The cursed castle is full of terrible things, but it sits in a forest long left untouched where good timber can still be found. Sometimes I go there to cut wood and salvage usable pieces from broken remains. If you go to the castle and find good timber, could you bring some back for me?
Demon bats are the bane of my existence. Every blue moon one of those bastards make it out of their god forsaken hole and wreck havoc on plot. Do me a favor and help me locate where they come from.
I used to have a keen sense to detect demonic auras in my youth. Alas, these days that skill has gone to waste. I am curious if you can replicate my odd abilities.
That forsaken castle has become the final resting ground for too many overconfident adventurers. I’m not saying you’re the same as the rest but I’d be surprised if you could survive more than once.
The demonic aura coming from the depths of the castle are so powerful that even my waning abilities can sense them. We need a hero to cleanse the air.
Nothing better to test your fire making skills in the most inhospitable environment known to man. Get to it! Practice makes perfect.
The giant folk have been making trouble on the peaks. Clear the way for other adventurers and search parties by showing them who’s boss.
Something has gotten into the beasts on the frozen peaks. They have been exhibiting more aggression than before. It’s time to put an end to their menace.
I’ve heard that the depths of the Frost Mountain hold a dangerous secret. Can you explore it and let me know what you find?
It’s time to make those ghastly beasts pay for the chaos they’ve unleashed on the mountains.
I’ve heard that the frost demons have enlisted even more legendary creatures to do their biddings. Bring me proof of their existence.

Please investigate the bridges of the Forgotten Castle and the site where the ritual, tainted by darkness, was once performed. I've heard rumors that if one lingers there for too long, the screams of someone unseen can be heard. I need to know whether this is truth or mere superstition.

There is something I need to find in the Forgotten Castle. But first, the path must be cleared. Beasts and vermin tainted by darkness block the way, and my strength alone is not enough to handle them... Could you eliminate these creatures for me?

I searched through every bookshelf in the Ruins, but with my dull senses, I couldn’t find a single thing. This isn’t good... I was promised something in exchange for retrieving those books for the Alchemist, something I must obtain. Could you search for the books in my stead? Please, I’m counting on you.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Woodsman_Title_05_: The Use of a Forgotten Castle
DC.Text_DesignData_Religion_Religion_Blytha: Blythar embodies the art of deception and unpredictability, viewing life as a complex chessboard. His followers, known as the Veils, use cunning and manipulation to navigate through life's trials. They champion adaptability and the clever use of deceit as tools to outmaneuver foes and overcome obstacles, often blurring the lines of morality to secure their victories.
DC.Text_DesignData_Religion_Religion_Noxulo: Noxulon represents judgment through darkness, asserting that embracing the shadow is crucial for peace. His teachings delve into deeper, darker realms centered on the pursuit of dark pleasures and ruthless self-gratification. His followers employ any means necessary, from sacrifice to deceit, even murder, to achieve personal power, discarding traditional morals in favor of their own desires.
DC.Text_DesignData_Religion_Religion_Solari: Lightbringers champion the purifying power of light, advocating that righteousness alone can dispel corruption. This faction is committed to an unyielding pursuit of justice, often adopting radical measures to eliminate what they perceive as darkness. These adherents believe they are enacting a celestial mandate, striving to bring justice and virtue wherever shadows fall. Their actions are shaped by this profound belief, pushing them to sacrifice personal peace for the greater good under the radiant guidance of Solaris.
DC.Text_DesignData_Religion_Religion_ZorinD: Zorin, the deity of wisdom and arcane knowledge, guides his followers to seek truth through the mysteries of the universe. This pursuit leads them into forbidden realms, where they harness esoteric powers at great personal risk. The Seekers believe in pushing the boundaries of knowledge, even venturing into morally ambiguous practices to unveil ancient secrets.

DC.Text_UI_WB_TomeOfKnowledge_Desc_02:
<Gold>Adventure, Normal, Squires to Riches, High-Roller, and Arena Modes</>
When selecting a campaign to play, you can choose between Adventure and Normal modes. The Squires to Riches and High-Roller modes appear as their own campaign book and places adventurers into a random dungeon. Finally, the Arena mode is available as a special campaign during limited times.

▪ Adventure Mode (Online PvE only mode) - A more traditional co-op dungeon crawling experience where you can go in with friends to navigate the dungeons and escape with good loot. - This mode focuses on exploration and adventuring in the dungeons without the worries of PvP.

▪ Normal Mode (PvP Enabled) - This mode ups the difficulty by enabling PvP encounters in the dungeons. An item gear cap ensures that fights against other players don’t become too lopsided. The extra risks bring greater rewards with better quality loot to be found in this mode.

▪ Squires to Riches Mode (PvP Enabled) - A party focused PvP mode where everyone starts the adventure in low-end gear. Scramble to find the best loot and secure one of the limited random portals to extract with your newfound riches.

▪ High-Roller Mode (PvP Enabled) - The ultimate test of survival in the dungeons for the highest quality loot. These environments are extremely dangerous with much tougher monsters and the most powerful gear permitted for opposing adventurers. An all-encompassing Dark Swarm forces desperate adventurers into tighter quarters as the adventure progresses. With highly limited extracts, only the most cunning and ruthless adventurers can survive these dungeons. This mode quickly places adventurers into a randomly selected dungeon.

▪ Arena Mode - A 3vs3 competitive PvP mode without any extraction mechanics. Teams of adventurers fight against each other to prove their combat prowess. Adventurers are ranked based on the outcome of their battles to climb a seasonal leaderboard. This mode is only open during limited times.

Extracting from the dungeons. When the timer expires on each map, any players still in the dungeon will die, so you will need to find a way to escape using various extract methods. Each map has different extraction points that become available to adventurers throughout the course of the session. Every map has multiple extraction methods, from solo stairs and rope escapes, to team portal pedestals and elevator escapes. In the ‘Adventure’ and ‘Normal’ modes, these extraction points are indicated on the maps by their blue icons. In the ‘Squires to Riches’ and ‘High-Roller’ modes, extraction portals appear from the ground as the adventure progresses with fixed extraction points being much rarer.

DC.Text_UI_WB_TomeOfKnowledge_Desc_05:
<Gold>Healing</>
Healing comes in various forms, and is broken down into health and recoverable health.

▪ Health can be restored by Health Potions and Surgical Kits, Health Shrines, or Resting at a Campfire. Warlocks can also recover their own health with some of their spells, and Clerics are able to heal both themselves and other adventurers with a variety of healing spells. Clerics can even heal non-party members by targeting other players with their healing spells, so be careful not to heal an enemy by mistake!

▪ When taking damage, a portion of the damage taken is shown as Recoverable Health, represented by the grey-red health on the HP bar. Using the Rest (G) command will cause your character to sit and slowly recover this health. Recoverable health can also be quickly healed by using Bandages. Druids can also restore Recoverable Health using certain spells.

<Gold>Spell Recovery</>
Spells that have charges can be recovered by Resting (G). The speed at which a spell will recover charges depends on the tier of the spell. Low tier spells will recovery very quickly, while high tier spells can take a long time to regenerate while resting. Like health, spell recovery speed is also affected by stats, the Spell Recovery Bonus can be seen in your character stat page. While Resting at Campfires, spell recovery is greatly increased, so magic users with spell charges are encouraged to keep one handy to help them stay prepared for fights in the dungeon. The higher the quality of the Campfire, the longer it lasts, which means more Health and Spell recovery.

DC.Text_UI_WB_TomeOfKnowledge_Desc_06:
<Gold>Loot in the Dungeon</>
In the Dungeon, you will find various kinds of trinkets and treasures, as well as monster items. The quality of the items influences how much they will sell for to the various vendors - see the Merchant page to learn more about what to do with your loot. Some items may be required to complete quests, or used to craft gear which becomes available when you raise your affinity with merchants through completing quests. These items must be “looted” status, meaning you extracted from the dungeon with them. Taking them back into the dungeons, trading them, or buying them from the market will changed them to “handled” status, which will prevent them from being valid turn-ins for quests. Ores and Ingots are the exceptions to this.
DC.Text_DataAsset_Luck_Desc_LuckDesc: Improves your chance to uncover better quality items.
DC.Text_UI_WB_TomeOfKnowledge_Desc_07:
<Gold>The Trader’s Guild</>
The market is split into two sections, the Marketplace and Trade Hall. To gain access to the Trader’s guild, you must be level 20 and pay a fee of 25 Gold to become a trader. Squire accounts have a limited license to use the Market, and can only purchase items from the Marketplace. Legendary accounts are able to sell and buy items.

▪ Marketplace: The Marketplace works as a place to list items for sale at a fixed price. Players can navigate to the “My Listings” tab, then click on an item in their inventory or stash, and choose a price to list the item. A minimum 15 gold tax is applied to all sales on the Marketplace, after 100 gold, a 5% listing fee is applied to all sales. Items listed on the Marketplace expire after 7 days, and must be retrieved from the listings tab within 7 days of expiration, or they will be lost. Successful sales are granted a 14 day retrieval period. Items purchased from the Marketplace are placed in the player’s inventory, or stash if there is no room.

▪ Trade Hall: The Trade Hall is a way to trade directly with another player. All trades performed in the Trade Hall are subject to a 15 gold tax from both players. Items can be linked in the chat using Shift-Click.

DC.Text_UI_WB_TomeOfKnowledge_Desc_03:
<Gold>Quests</>
At the beginning of a new wipe, each merchant will have quests available to the player - quests are linked to an account and quest progression carries over across all characters on a single account. Over the course of the wipe, more quests will unlock. Quests require the player to visit various maps to complete objectives, like collecting certain items, defeating various types of enemies or bosses, and even other adventurers. Completing these quests will raise your affinity with the merchant, and reward you with gold, equipment, or in some cases very rare and useful items. 


<Gold>Affinity</>
Raising your affinity with merchants through quests unlocks a number of benefits - each stage of affinity gives you discounts when purchasing from them, increases the rarity and number of items they will sell, and unlock new crafting recipes that refresh periodically. Affinity is shared with all of the characters on your account, allowing you to craft gear and purchase higher quality equipment from any character. This also allows the player to access higher tier baseline equipment at the Squire.


<Gold>Crafting</>
When your affinity is high enough with merchants, you will be able to bring certain items like ingots, powders, and monster items to craft powerful equipment with specific stats that are unique to the merchant, and cannot be obtained in the dungeon. The base stats on the craftable items is always guaranteed, but the affixes are random with each craft. Some merchant crafts even offer weapons with increased power against monsters in the dungeon, or named weapons with new stats that enable interesting builds.

DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsLink_Desc:
To honor our commitment to loyal Blacksmith supporters who purchased the game before it became available on a mainstream platform, we wish to ensure that those players can switch their accounts to a mainstream platform such as Epic Games and Steam if they choose to do so.
Players who purchased the Dark and Darker Standard / Founders: Hold the Line Edition on the Blacksmith platform before June 7, 2024 (UTC) have a one-time opportunity to permanently transfer their account to the Epic Game Store or Steam platform of their choice.
Eligible players can do this by generating a ‘Migration Code’ and then entering it when creating an account on the new platform.

Instructions on transferring this account to a new platform.
1. Generate a temporary unique ‘Migration Code’ by pressing the ‘Get Migration Code’ button. The code will appear hidden to protect your account. DO NOT REVEAL THIS CODE TO ANYONE.
2. Press the ‘Copy’ button to have the code copied to your system memory.
3. Close the game and then open Dark and Darker on the new platform you wish to link this account.

Transferring the account to a brand-new platform with no characters created.
a. If the new platform has no account associated with it (i.e. no character was ever created), then a ‘Legacy Blacksmith Users’ popup will appear when you log into the game. Click the "Transfer" button and Paste the copied Migration Code when prompted. Once you successfully transfer an account you will advance to the platform selection screen for final platform selection.
b. if you can see the platform selection screen, choose one you wish to use from now on. If the platform you select differs from the one you are currently connected to, the game client will be closed. Then, kindly restart the game from the selected platform.
c. "Transfer my Blacksmith Account" is complete.

Transferring the account to a platform that you accidentally created a character on.
a. If you accidentally created a character on the new platform, you need to first delete ALL characters on the new platform before transferring your original account. You can delete a character by going to the main ‘Character Select’ menu and pressing the ‘Delete Character’ button.
b. Once all characters are deleted on the account restart the game on the new platform and follow the instructions above.
<ImportantText>c. It is not possible to link a previous account to the new platform account if DLC(like Legendary Status) or Redstones were ever purchased on the new platform account, even if all characters have been removed. We recommend creating another account on the new platform if you wish to transfer to that platform in this instance.</>

DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA02_Demigod_Flavor: Its icy exterior shimmers with a celestial glow, promising a taste of the frost-kissed wonders that lie within.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA02_Exemplar_Flavor: Casting a captivating display of frost and fire, its glacial blue flames flicker with an otherworldly allure, transforming any campsite into a mystical sanctuary amidst the frozen wilderness.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA02_Pathfinder_Flavor: From the icy depths of death, this undead monstrosity trudges forth, spreading the cold touch of doom.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA02_Voyager_Flavor: This flame is rumored to be forged from the tears of winter spirits and infused with the essence of ancient frost dragons, imbuing it with an aura both chilling and enchanting.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA03_Demigod_Flavor: Pulsating with sinister dark energies that thirst to unleash their malevolent influence, this heart mirrors the corruption that consumed the mighty King of the Forgotten Castle in his pursuit of immortality. What hidden darkness will it awaken in you?
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA03_Exemplar_Flavor: Emitting the colors of the ancient Elven woods, this magical fire fills the air with an irresistible mix of herbal scents and sweet aromas from their revered trees, enchanting every traveler who draws near.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA03_Pathfinder_Flavor: Once a valiant knight, the Skeleton Champion earned his medal through unmatched prowess and unwavering loyalty to the now, Ghost King. In life, he fought bravely before his sovereign; in death, he remains a spectral warrior, eternally bound to the echoes of his king’s command.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA03_Voyager_Flavor: As you rest, you carve a wooden doll, every cut filled with memories of home and the hope of gifting it to a loved one, provided you make it out alive...
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA04_Demigod_Flavor: Eyes hollow, bones splintered, yet they march—a procession of anguish bound by eternal war.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA04_Exemplar_Flavor: There’s something satisfying about surveying and organizing your spoils; each treasure has its place, and every piece tells a story.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA04_Pathfinder_Flavor: Devoid of life yet unyielding, it shuffles beneath a shroud of rot. The stench of decay lingers, brittle bones exposed to the ravages of time.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA04_Voyager_Flavor: A green, bubbling brew churns within the cauldron, reeking of rot and despair. Its stench twists the stomach and lingers in the mind.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA05_Demigod_Flavor: Kneel in reverence and offer your devotion to a true champion of the dungeons.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA05_Exemplar_Flavor: Take a rest and get sucked into the ancient pages of the Abyssal Grimoire. Be cautious when reciting any of these unorthodox incantations, you never know what might occur.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA05_Pathfinder_Flavor: Risen from the depths of the Inferno, the Nightmare Skeleton Crossbowman is relentless with its aim, each bolt striking with deadly precision.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA05_Voyager_Flavor: An eerie torch with no flame, instead only one brightly glowing red gemstone salvaged from the abyssal depths of hell’s blood lakes themselves.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_2_Demigod_Flavor: Your insatiable curiosity for the Ruins knows no bounds. As if under a spell, you find yourself drawn again and again to these forsaken places.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_2_Exemplar_Flavor: Crafted from the remains of an ancient lich, this torch carries a sinister legacy. Its flames flicker with a deep unnatural glow, reflecting the souls it once devoured.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_2_Pathfinder_Flavo: Cursed for hunting the Midnight Stag, this lycan’s inner savagery has been amplified, compelling it to feel an overwhelming urge to destroy all it sees, whether friend or foe.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_2_Voyager_Flavor: Awaken the beast within, and let loose a howl that echoes through the lands, calling out to friends or serving as a warning to foes.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_Demigod_Flavor: The banner that bears the might of the Black Despair. This ruthless crew does not hide their brutality. They flaunt it, feeding on the fear of others. In their wake remain only blazing fires, shattered wreckage, and this banner.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_Exemplar_Flavor: Relax in true buccaneer fashion, seated with a spyglass, ever on the lookout for treasures, threats, and new horizons.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_Pathfinder_Flavor: This corpse, long submerged in the sea, leaks foul water with every step, leaving behind a trail of sticky footprints.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA06_Voyager_Flavor: With a mystical fire that defies water's touch, its flickering light reflecting off the herring scales, transforming any campsite into a coastal retreat.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA07_Demigod_Flavor: Faint embers trail across the sash, leaving a subtle red mark in their wake. The lingering heat within the dying sparks imparts a gentle warmth to its bearer.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA07_Exemplar_Flavor: It is a dance that strikes the ground with powerful steps to show the strength of one’s legs. Dwarves enliven it with lively claps and simple repeating chants. When one dancer begins, the others soon join and it can become a celebration that lasts for hours.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA07_Pathfinder_Flavor: Ifrits are beings born of fire. With flames for hair, they possess an inherently destructive nature. This disposition extends even to their own kind, so they do not form groups and instead live independently.
DC.Text_Reward_Rank_EA07_Voyager_Flavor: A campfire shaped in the likeness of a small volcano. When kindled, red lava bursts from its crater yet despite its convincing appearance it carries only a gentle warmth and gives no cause for fear.

DC.Text_Reward_Religion_Common_EA04_Flavor: This skeleton wanders the frozen depths of Frost Mountain, its cold bones creaking with every step.
DC.Text_Reward_Religion_Common_EA05_Flavor: This creature has crawled up from the dark, sunless depths of the abyss. The Nightmare Seawalker’s lifeless violet eyes emit a chilling gleam when it locks onto its prey.

DC.Text_Reward_Religion_Common_TidestoneOre: A dirty chunk of rock bearing traces of Tidestone with teal wave-like patterns.

Exit the game.

1) Launch the game in "Blacksmith" and click "Transfer My Account".
(You must use a new Blacksmith Account to make the transfer)
2) Enter the migration code and click "Link Account".
3) Click "Done", then the game will close itself. Please restart the game.
4) See you in the dungeon!

DC.Text_UI_WB_LeaderboardDetailPopup_Desc_N:
- Earn a ‘Seasonal Title’ through the dungeons.​

- Your Title is determined by the amount of Adventure Points (AP)
   you accumulate during the season.​

- A separate ‘Title’ is calculated for each dungeon.
   Your highest title is always displayed for your adventurer.​

- Earn AP by killing monsters, enemy players, opening chests and
   escaping the dungeons.
   AP is also determined by the value of the treasure loot that you
   extract from the dungeons.
   Going deeper into the dungeons, killing bosses and sub-bosses,
   and looting rare chests give higher AP. ​

- An AP entry fee is subtracted from your total based on
   your current Title each time you enter a dungeon. ​

- Your in-game name and border will reflect your highest seasonal title.​
DC.Text_UI_WB_LoadingScreen_Loading_Tooltip:
Use your torch to light up dark areas.
Use the mouse right-click to throw your torch.

Aim for the Head! Headshots do extra damage!
Attacks to the limbs do the least damage.

You can revive a teammate if they die. Collect their ‘soul heart’ from their corpse after removing their chest armor.
Find a sacrificial altar with their ‘soul heart’ equipped and make a small blood sacrifice.

A portal closes as soon as someone passes through it.
Sometimes it’s better to let an enemy open a portal, then steal it for yourself!

To cast a spell as a magic caster, make sure you equip the 'Spell Memory' skill. Magic casters can select their spell in-game by 
holding down their 'Spell Memory' skill key. Equip a magic weapon and hold down the right mouse to cast your spell.
Sell the loot you collect in the dungeon to the right merchant to build up your coffers.

You must aim your shield to block an attack. Look up to block a downward slash. If an attack hits a body part that sticks 
out like the top of your head, you will still take damage even if the weapon bounces off your shield.

DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_ClothSimuat:
Enables or disables physics-based movement for clothing such as capes, robes, and fabrics.
When enabled, clothing responds naturally to movement for a more immersive appearance, but may impact performance.
When disabled, clothing is rendered in a fixed position to improve performance.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_CollectGPUC:
Enable or disable the collection of GPU crash data.
Enabling this option may lower game performance.
You must restart the game after changing settings.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_DirectXVers:
Select which rendering system (DirectX version) to use.
You must restart the game after changing settings.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_DisplayBrig:
Adjusts the overall brightness of the screen.
This setting helps improve visibility in dark environments or reduce eye strain in overly bright scenes.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_DisplayMode: Sets how the game is displayed on your screen.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_DisplayReso:
Sets the width and height of the game screen in pixels.
Higher resolutions provide sharper visuals but may reduce performance. Lower resolutions improve performance but may result in blurrier visuals.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_FrameRateMe:
Limits the maximum number of frames rendered per second while in the game lobby.
Helps reduce unnecessary resource usage, heat, and fan noise.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_FrameRate_D:
Limits the maximum number of frames rendered per second.
Capping the frame rate can reduce GPU load and heat, helping to maintain consistent performance and prevent screen tearing.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_PostProcess:
Adjusts post-processing effects such as bloom, color grading, and depth of field.
Lower settings minimize screen effects to improve performance, while higher settings enhance visual immersion with advanced effects.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_RenderScale:
Manually adjusts the ratio between rendering resolution and screen resolution.
Lower values improve performance but reduce image clarity, while higher values enhance sharpness at the cost of performance.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_ShadowQuali:
Adjusts the resolution and detail level of shadows generated by in-game lighting.
Lower settings simplify or disable shadows for better performance, while higher settings provide more realistic and detailed shadow rendering.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_TextureQual:
Controls the resolution of textures applied to characters, environments, and items.
Lower settings reduce memory usage but may cause textures to appear blurry, while higher settings render materials with greater detail.
DC.Text_UI_WB_MenuOptionsVideos_VisualEffec:
Sets the quality and rendering range of visual effects such as spells, status effects, and damage impacts during combat.
Lower settings simplify effects and reduce rendering distance for better performance, while higher settings provide richer visuals and a higher rendering distance for immersive combat.

DC.Text_UI_WB_Login_WelcomeText:
Early Access Hotfix #94
Early Access 2nd Anniversary Event and upcoming Semi-Semi-Wipe.

Hi Adventurers,
This minor update brings the 2nd anniversary event for the Early Access release. The ‘Skeleton’ has returned to the tavern to drop some tasty new quests for this event. We’ve also added some minor optimization and bugfixes to improve your experience.

We know that the next season will be critical for the longevity of the game and therefore we made the difficult decision to delay the next season rather than push out a rushed update.

We are sorry to announce that the next season will need to be delayed one month to September 23. Unfortunately, the reality is that our two main features for the next season, a brand new water-themed dungeon and the social Gathering Hall system, still need more work. Although we’ve been making good progress with both features, we need more time to get them to an acceptable quality for the upcoming ‘make or break' season. 

We are very sorry for this delay and realize that this may take some wind out of the current player-base. As a mea-culpa and amends, we’ve worked on an urgent plan to make the remaining time leading up to the next season a little more interesting and meaningful. On August 26, we will be doing a ‘Semi-Semi-Wipe’ which will commence a super condensed mini-season known as ‘EA Season 6.9'. It will basically function as a season without the addition of a season defining feature. Instead the ‘Semi-Semi-Wipe’ will include the following.
- SSF mode for the first two weeks of the mini season. The marketplace and trading post will only become available for the last 2 weeks of the mini season. 
- All character levels, items, inventory, quests, and affinity will be reset.
- A new condensed Adventure Rank season with rewards.
- A new Arena season with new maps in the Arena map pool. 
- A new religion season with rewards.

We thank you for your understanding as we work our butts off to turn the tide and bring you a good foundational update for the September 23rd launch. Thank you and see you in the dungeons.
